2.37.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
kathaṃ dāruvanaṃ prāpto bhagavān govṛṣadhvajaḥ /
mohayāmāsa viprendrān sūta vaktumihārhasi //
2.37.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः
कथं दारुवनं प्राप्तो भगवान् गोवृषध्वजः ।
मोहयामास विप्रेन्द्रान् सूत वक्तुमिहार्हसि ॥
2.37.m: The seers said: / How did the blessed Lord whose emblem is the bull reach the Dāru forest / and delude the eminent brahmins? O Sūta, you should tell this here.

2.37.s:
sūta uvāca
purā dāruvan ramye devasiddhaniṣevite /
saputradārā munayastapaśceruḥ sahasraśaḥ //
2.37.d:
सूत उवाच
पुरा दारुवन् रम्ये देवसिद्धनिषेविते ।
सपुत्रदारा मुनयस्तपश्चेरुः सहस्रशः ॥
2.37.m: Sūta said: / Formerly, in the lovely Dāru forest frequented by gods and siddhas, / thousands of sages with their sons and wives practiced asceticism.

2.37.s:
pravṛttaṃ vividhaṃ karma prakurvāṇā yathāvidhi /
yajanti vividhairyajñaistapanti ca maharṣayaḥ //
2.37.d:
प्रवृत्तं विविधं कर्म प्रकुर्वाणा यथाविधि ।
यजन्ति विविधैर्यज्ञैस्तपन्ति च महर्षयः ॥
2.37.m: Performing various active rituals according to rule, / the great seers sacrificed with various sacrifices and practiced tapas.

2.37.s:
teṣāṃ pravṛttivinyastacetasāmatha śūladhṛk /
khyāpayan sa mahādoṣaṃ yayau dāruvanaṃ haraḥ //
2.37.d:
तेषां प्रवृत्तिविन्यस्तचेतसामथ शूलधृक् ।
ख्यापयन् स महादोषं ययौ दारुवनं हरः ॥
2.37.m: Then, to those whose minds were settled in the path of active ritual, Hara, the trident-bearer, / went to the Dāru forest, showing the great fault [therein].

2.37.s:
kṛtvā viśvaguruṃ viṣṇuṃ pārśve devo maheśvaraḥ /
yayau nivṛttavijñānasthāpanārthaṃ ca śaṅkaraḥ //
2.37.d:
कृत्वा विश्वगुरुं विष्णुं पार्श्वे देवो महेश्वरः ।
ययौ निवृत्तविज्ञानस्थापनार्थं च शङ्करः ॥
2.37.m: Having placed Viṣṇu, the teacher of the universe, at his side, the god Maheśvara, / Śaṅkara, went in order to establish the knowledge of detachment.

2.37.s:
āsthāya vipulaṃ veśamūnaviṃśativatsaraḥ /
līlālaso mahābāhuḥ pīnāṅgaścārulocanaḥ //
2.37.d:
आस्थाय विपुलं वेशमूनविंशतिवत्सरः ।
लीलालसो महाबाहुः पीनाङ्गश्चारुलोचनः ॥
2.37.m: Assuming an imposing appearance, nineteen years of age, / languid with playfulness, large-armed, plump-limbed, and handsome-eyed,

2.37.s:
cāmīkaravapuḥ śrīmān pūrṇacandranibhānanaḥ /
mattamātaṅgagāmano digvāsā jagadīśvaraḥ //
2.37.d:
चामीकरवपुः श्रीमान् पूर्णचन्द्रनिभाननः ।
मत्तमातङ्गगामनो दिग्वासा जगदीश्वरः ॥
2.37.m: possessing a body of gold, glorious, with a face like the full moon, / walking like an elephant in rut, sky-clad, the Lord of the world,

2.37.s:
kuśeśayamayīṃ mālaṃ sarvaratnairalaṅkṛtām /
dadhāno bhagavānīśaḥ samāgacchati sasmitaḥ //
2.37.d:
कुशेशयमयीं मालं सर्वरत्नैरलङ्कृताम् ।
दधानो भगवानीशः समागच्छति सस्मितः ॥
2.37.m: wearing a garland made of blue lotuses adorned with all kinds of jewels, / the blessed Lord arrived with a smile.

2.37.s:
yo 'nantaḥ puruṣo yonirlokānāmavyayo hariḥ /
strīveṣaṃ viṣṇurāsthāya so 'nugacchati śūlinam //
2.37.d:
यो ऽनन्तः पुरुषो योनिर्लोकानामव्ययो हरिः ।
स्त्रीवेषं विष्णुरास्थाय सो ऽनुगच्छति शूलिनम् ॥
2.37.m: Hari, the imperishable, infinite Person, the source of the worlds— / Viṣṇu, assuming the attire of a woman, followed the trident-bearer:

2.37.s:
sampūrṇacandravadanaṃ pīnonnatapayodharam /
śucismitaṃ suprasannaṃ raṇannupurakadvayam //
2.37.d:
सम्पूर्णचन्द्रवदनं पीनोन्नतपयोधरम् ।
शुचिस्मितं सुप्रसन्नं रणन्नुपुरकद्वयम् ॥
2.37.m: having a face like the full moon, plump and elevated breasts, / a bright smile, very radiant, with a pair of tinkling anklets,

2.37.s:
supītavasanaṃ divyaṃ śyāmalaṃ cārulocanam /
udārahaṃsacalanaṃ vilāsi sumanoharam //
2.37.d:
सुपीतवसनं दिव्यं श्यामलं चारुलोचनम् ।
उदारहंसचलनं विलासि सुमनोहरम् ॥
2.37.m: with divine, fine yellow garments, dark-complexioned, beautiful-eyed, / moving with the noble gait of a swan, playful, and exceedingly charming.

2.37.s:
evaṃ sa bhagavānīśo devadāruvane haraḥ /
cacāra hariṇā bhikṣāṃ māyayā mohayan jagat //
2.37.d:
एवं स भगवानीशो देवदारुवने हरः ।
चचार हरिणा भिक्षां मायया मोहयन् जगत् ॥
2.37.m: Thus did the blessed Lord Hara roam for alms in the Devadāru forest / with Hari, deluding the world by illusory creative power.

2.37.s:
dṛṣṭvā carantaṃ viśveśaṃ tatra tatra pinākinam /
māyayā mohitā nāryo devadevaṃ samanvayuḥ //
2.37.d:
दृष्ट्वा चरन्तं विश्वेशं तत्र तत्र पिनाकिनम् ।
मायया मोहिता नार्यो देवदेवं समन्वयुः ॥
2.37.m: Seeing the Lord of the universe, the wielder of the Pināka, roaming here and there, / women deluded by illusory creative power followed the God of gods.

2.37.s:
vistrastavastrābharaṇāstyaktvā lajjāṃ pativratāḥ /
sahaiva tena kāmārtā vilāsinyaścarantihi //
2.37.d:
विस्त्रस्तवस्त्राभरणास्त्यक्त्वा लज्जां पतिव्रताः ।
सहैव तेन कामार्ता विलासिन्यश्चरन्तिहि ॥
2.37.m: With clothes and ornaments slipping off, casting aside shame, those devoted wives, / distressed with desire and acting playfully, roamed along with him.

2.37.s:
ṛṣīṇāṃ putrakā ye syuryuvāno jitamānasāḥ /
anvagacchan hṛṣīkeśaṃ sarve kāmaprapīḍitāḥ //
2.37.d:
ऋषीणां पुत्रका ये स्युर्युवानो जितमानसाः ।
अन्वगच्छन् हृषीकेशं सर्वे कामप्रपीडिताः ॥
2.37.m: The youthful sons of the sages who had subdued their minds, / overcome with desire, all followed Hṛṣīkeśa.

2.37.s:
gāyanti nṛtyanti vilāsabāhyā
nārīgaṇā māyinamekamīśam /
dṛṣṭvā sapatnīkamatīvakānta-
micchantyathāliṅganamācaranti //
2.37.d:
गायन्ति नृत्यन्ति विलासबाह्या
नारीगणा मायिनमेकमीशम् ।
दृष्ट्वा सपत्नीकमतीवकान्त-
मिच्छन्त्यथालिङ्गनमाचरन्ति ॥
2.37.m: Bereft of restraint, groups of women sang and danced / [before] the one Lord who wields illusory creative power; / seeing him accompanied by a wife and exceedingly handsome, / they desired and embraced him.

2.37.s:
pade nipetuḥ smitamācaranti
gāyanti gītāni munīśaputrāḥ /
ālokya padmāpatimādidevaṃ
bhrūbhaṅgamanye vicaranti tena //
2.37.d:
पदे निपेतुः स्मितमाचरन्ति
गायन्ति गीतानि मुनीशपुत्राः ।
आलोक्य पद्मापतिमादिदेवं
भ्रूभङ्गमन्ये विचरन्ति तेन ॥
2.37.m: The sons of the lordly sages fell at his feet, smiled, / and sang songs; / beholding the primal god, the lord of Padmā, / some reacted to him with knit eyebrows.

2.37.s:
āsāmathaiṣāmapi vāsudevo
māyī murārirmanasi praviṣṭaḥ /
karoti bhogān manasi pravṛttiṃ
māyānubhūyanta itiva samyak //
2.37.d:
आसामथैषामपि वासुदेवो
मायी मुरारिर्मनसि प्रविष्टः ।
करोति भोगान् मनसि प्रवृत्तिं
मायानुभूयन्त इतिव सम्यक् ॥
2.37.m: Then Vāsudeva, the deceptive foe of Mura, entered into the minds / of both these [women and men]; / he generated pleasures and impulses in their minds, / as though the illusory creations were genuinely experienced.

2.37.s:
vibhāti viśvāmarabhūtabhartā
sa mādhavaḥ strīgaṇamadhyaviṣṭaḥ /
aśeṣaśaktyāsanasaṃniviṣṭo
yathaikaśaktyā saha devadevaḥ //
2.37.d:
विभाति विश्वामरभूतभर्ता
स माधवः स्त्रीगणमध्यविष्टः ।
अशेषशक्त्यासनसंनिविष्टो
यथैकशक्त्या सह देवदेवः ॥
2.37.m: Mādhava, the sustainer of the universe, gods, and beings, shone / having entered the midst of the troop of women, / seated on the throne of all powers, / just as the God of gods [shines] with his single power.

2.37.s:
karoti nṛtyaṃ paramaprabhāvaṃ
tadā virūḍhaḥ punareva bhūyaḥ /
yayau samāruhya hariḥ svabhāvaṃ
tadīśavṛttāmṛtamādidevaḥ //
2.37.d:
करोति नृत्यं परमप्रभावं
तदा विरूढः पुनरेव भूयः ।
ययौ समारुह्य हरिः स्वभावं
तदीशवृत्तामृतमादिदेवः ॥
2.37.m: Then, having grown once more, he performs a dance of supreme majesty. / Hari, the primeval god, having assumed his own nature, departed upon that nectar of the Lord's conduct.

2.37.s:
dṛṣṭvā nārīkulaṃ rudraṃ putrāṇāmapi keśavam /
mohayantaṃ muniśreṣṭhāḥ kopaṃ saṃdadhire bhṛśam //
2.37.d:
दृष्ट्वा नारीकुलं रुद्रं पुत्राणामपि केशवम् ।
मोहयन्तं मुनिश्रेष्ठाः कोपं संदधिरे भृशम् ॥
2.37.m: Seeing Rudra bewitching the multitude of women and Keśava bewitching the sons, / the foremost sages fell into a violent rage.

2.37.s:
atīva paruṣaṃ vākyaṃ procurdevaṃ kapardinam /
śeṣuśca śāpairvividhairmāyayā tasya mohitāḥ //
2.37.d:
अतीव परुषं वाक्यं प्रोचुर्देवं कपर्दिनम् ।
शेषुश्च शापैर्विविधैर्मायया तस्य मोहिताः ॥
2.37.m: They spoke extremely harsh words to the matted-haired god, / and, deluded by his illusory creative power, cursed him with various curses.

2.37.s:
tapāṃsi teṣāṃ sarveṣāṃ pratyāhanyanta śaṅkare /
yathādityaprakāśena tārakā nabhasi sthitāḥ //
2.37.d:
तपांसि तेषां सर्वेषां प्रत्याहन्यन्त शङ्करे ।
यथादित्यप्रकाशेन तारका नभसि स्थिताः ॥
2.37.m: All their ascetic practices were shattered upon Śaṅkara, / just like the stars situated in the sky by the radiance of the sun.

2.37.s:
te bhagnatapaso viprāḥ sametya vṛṣabhadhvajam /
ko bhavāniti deveśaṃ pṛcchanti sma vimohitāḥ //
2.37.d:
ते भग्नतपसो विप्राः समेत्य वृषभध्वजम् ।
को भवानिति देवेशं पृच्छन्ति स्म विमोहिताः ॥
2.37.m: Those Brahmins whose austerities were broken approached the bull-bannered god; / deluded, they asked the Lord of gods: “Who are you?”

2.37.s:
so 'bravīd bhagavānīśastapaścartumihāgataḥ /
idānīṃ bhāryayā deśe bhavadbhiriha suvratāḥ //
2.37.d:
सो ऽब्रवीद् भगवानीशस्तपश्चर्तुमिहागतः ।
इदानीं भार्यया देशे भवद्भिरिह सुव्रताः ॥
2.37.m: [Brahmā] said: “The Lord, the Sovereign, came here to practice austerities / in this place with his wife, O men of virtuous vows, [just seen] by you.

2.37.s:
tasya te vākyamākarṇya bhṛgvādyā munipuṅgavāḥ /
ūcurgṛhītvā vasanaṃ tyaktvā bhāryāṃ tapaścara //
2.37.d:
तस्य ते वाक्यमाकर्ण्य भृग्वाद्या मुनिपुङ्गवाः ।
ऊचुर्गृहीत्वा वसनं त्यक्त्वा भार्यां तपश्चर ॥
2.37.m:
Hearing his words, the eminent sages headed by Bhṛgu
said: "Take a garment, abandon your wife, and practice austerity!"

2.37.s:
athovāca vihasyeśaḥ pinākī nīlalohitaḥ /
saṃprekṣya jagato yoniṃ pārśvasthaṃ ca janārdanam //
2.37.d:
अथोवाच विहस्येशः पिनाकी नीललोहितः ।
संप्रेक्ष्य जगतो योनिं पार्श्वस्थं च जनार्दनम् ॥
2.37.m:
Then the Lord, the wielder of the Pināka, the blue-and-red one, laughed and spoke,
looking upon the origin of the world and upon Janārdana standing at his side:

2.37.s:
kathaṃ bhavadbhiruditaṃ svabhāryāpoṣaṇotsukaiḥ /
tyaktavyā mama bhāryeti dharmajñaiḥ śāntamānasaiḥ //
2.37.d:
कथं भवद्भिरुदितं स्वभार्यापोषणोत्सुकैः ।
त्यक्तव्या मम भार्येति धर्मज्ञैः शान्तमानसैः ॥
2.37.m:
"How is it that you, who are eager to maintain your own wives,
who know duty, and whose minds are peaceful, say that my wife should be abandoned?"

2.37.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
vyabhicāraratā nāryaḥ saṃtyājyāḥ patineritāḥ /
asmābhireṣā subhagā tādṛśī tyāgamarhati //
2.37.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः
व्यभिचाररता नार्यः संत्याज्याः पतिनेरिताः ।
अस्माभिरेषा सुभगा तादृशी त्यागमर्हति ॥
2.37.m:
The sages said:
"Women devoted to adultery should be abandoned, so the husbands have declared.
We have seen that this lovely woman is such a one; she deserves abandonment."

2.37.s:
mahādeva uvāca
na kadācidiyaṃ viprā manasāpyanyamicchati /
nāhamenāmapi tathā vimuñcāmi kadācana //
2.37.d:
महादेव उवाच
न कदाचिदियं विप्रा मनसाप्यन्यमिच्छति ।
नाहमेनामपि तथा विमुञ्चामि कदाचन ॥
2.37.m:
Mahādeva said:
"O brāhmaṇas, she never desires another even in her mind,
nor do I ever abandon her in such a manner."

2.37.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
dṛṣṭvā vyabhicarantīha hyasmābhiḥ puruṣādhama /
uktaṃ hyasatyaṃ bhavatā gamyatāṃ kṣiprameva hi //
2.37.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः
दृष्ट्वा व्यभिचरन्तीह ह्यस्माभिः पुरुषाधम ।
उक्तं ह्यसत्यं भवता गम्यतां क्षिप्रमेव हि ॥
2.37.m:
The sages said:
"Having seen her committing adultery here, O lowest of men,
an untruth has indeed been spoken by you. Begone at once!"

2.37.s:
evamukte mahādevaḥ satyameva mayeritam /
bhavatāṃ pratibhātyeṣetyuktvāsau vicacāra ha //
2.37.d:
एवमुक्ते महादेवः सत्यमेव मयेरितम् ।
भवतां प्रतिभात्येषेत्युक्त्वासौ विचचार ह ॥
2.37.m:
When this was said, Mahādeva spoke:
"Only the truth was spoken by me; such is your impression." Having said this, he wandered on.

2.37.s:
so 'gacchaddhariṇā sārdhaṃ munindrasya mahātmanaḥ /
vasiṣṭhasyāśramaṃ puṇyaṃ bhikṣārtho parameśvaraḥ //
2.37.d:
सो ऽगच्छद्धरिणा सार्धं मुनिन्द्रस्य महात्मनः ।
वसिष्ठस्याश्रमं पुण्यं भिक्षार्थो परमेश्वरः ॥
2.37.m:
Together with Hari, he went to the holy hermitage of the great-souled sage,
the lord of sages, Vasiṣṭha, the Supreme Lord seeking alms.

2.37.s:
dṛṣṭvā samāgataṃ devaṃ bhikṣamāṇamarundhatī /
vasiṣṭhasya priyā bhāryā pratyudgamya nanāma nam //
2.37.d:
दृष्ट्वा समागतं देवं भिक्षमाणमरुन्धती ।
वसिष्ठस्य प्रिया भार्या प्रत्युद्गम्य ननाम नम् ॥
2.37.m:
Seeing the god arrived begging for alms, Arundhatī,
the beloved wife of Vasiṣṭha, came forward and bowed to him.

2.37.s:
prakṣālya pādau vimalaṃ dattvā cāsanamuttamam /
saṃprekṣya śithilaṃ gātramabhighātahataṃ dvijaiḥ /
saṃdhayāmāsa bhaiṣajyairviṣṇā vadanā satī //
2.37.d:
प्रक्षाल्य पादौ विमलं दत्त्वा चासनमुत्तमम् ।
संप्रेक्ष्य शिथिलं गात्रमभिघातहतं द्विजैः ।
संधयामास भैषज्यैर्विष्णा वदना सती ॥
2.37.m:
Washing his feet and offering him a spotless, excellent seat,
and seeing his body weakened, struck by the blows of the twice-born,
the virtuous woman, distressed in countenance, treated him with remedies.

2.37.s:
cakāra mahatīṃ pūjāṃ prārthayāmāsa bhāryayā /
ko bhavān kuta āyātaḥ kimācāro bhavāniti /
uvāca tāṃ mahādevaḥ siddhānāṃ pravaro 'smyaham //
2.37.d:
चकार महतीं पूजां प्रार्थयामास भार्यया ।
को भवान् कुत आयातः किमाचारो भवानिति ।
उवाच तां महादेवः सिद्धानां प्रवरो ऽस्म्यहम् ॥
2.37.m:
She performed great worship and inquired of him with his wife:
"Who are you? From where have you come? What is your way of conduct?"
Mahādeva said to her: "I am the foremost among the Siddhas.

2.37.s:
yadetanmaṇḍalaṃ śuddhaṃ bhāti brahmamayaṃ sadā /
eṣaiva devatā mahyaṃ dhārayāmi sadaiva tat //
2.37.d:
यदेतन्मण्डलं शुद्धं भाति ब्रह्ममयं सदा ।
एषैव देवता मह्यं धारयामि सदैव तत् ॥
2.37.m:
That which shines always as this pure realm consisting of Brahman—
that very thing is my deity; I bear that at all times."

2.37.s:
hatyuktvā prayayau śrīmānanugṛhya pativratām /
tāḍayāñcakrire daṇḍairloṣṭibhirmuṣṭibhidvijāḥ //
2.37.d:
हत्युक्त्वा प्रययौ श्रीमाननुगृह्य पतिव्रताम् ।
ताडयाञ्चक्रिरे दण्डैर्लोष्टिभिर्मुष्टिभिद्विजाः ॥
2.37.m:
Having said this, the glorious one departed, after bestowing favor upon the devoted wife.
The twice-born struck him with sticks, clods of earth, and fists.

2.37.s:
dṛṣṭvā carantaṃ giriśaṃ nagnaṃ vikṛtalakṣaṇam /
procuretad bhavāṃlliṅgamutpāṭayatu durmate //
2.37.d:
दृष्ट्वा चरन्तं गिरिशं नग्नं विकृतलक्षणम् ।
प्रोचुरेतद् भवांल्लिङ्गमुत्पाटयतु दुर्मते ॥
2.37.m:
Seeing Giriśa wandering naked with distorted features,
they said: "O wicked-minded one, tear off this liṅga!"

2.37.s:
tānabravīnmahāyogī kariṣyāmīti śaṅkaraḥ /
yuṣmākaṃ māmake liṅge yadi dveṣo 'bhijāyate //
2.37.d:
तानब्रवीन्महायोगी करिष्यामीति शङ्करः ।
युष्माकं मामके लिङ्गे यदि द्वेषो ऽभिजायते ॥
2.37.m:
The great yogin, Śaṅkara, said to them:
"I shall do so, if hatred has arisen among you toward my liṅga."

2.37.s:
ityuktvotpāṭayāmāsa bhagavān bhaganetrahā /
nāpaśyaṃstatkṣaṇeneśaṃ keśavaṃ liṅgameva ca //
2.37.d:
इत्युक्त्वोत्पाटयामास भगवान् भगनेत्रहा ।
नापश्यंस्तत्क्षणेनेशं केशवं लिङ्गमेव च ॥
2.37.m:
Having said this, the blessed one, the destroyer of Bhaga's eyes, tore it off.
In that instant, they did not see the Lord, nor Keśava, nor the liṅga.

2.37.s:
tadotpātā babhūvurhi lokānāṃ bhayaśaṃsinaḥ /
na rājate sahasrāṃśuścacāla pṛthivī punaḥ /
niṣprabhāśca grahāḥ sarve cukṣubhe ca mahodadhiḥ //
2.37.d:
तदोत्पाता बभूवुर्हि लोकानां भयशंसिनः ।
न राजते सहस्रांशुश्चचाल पृथिवी पुनः ।
निष्प्रभाश्च ग्रहाः सर्वे चुक्षुभे च महोदधिः ॥
2.37.m:
Then indeed portents portending fear for the worlds arose:
the thousand-rayed [sun] did not shine, the earth trembled repeatedly,
all the planets became lusterless, and the great ocean was agitated.

2.37.s:
apaśyaccānusūyātreḥ svapnaṃ bhāryā pativratā /
kathayāmāsa viprāṇāṃ bhayādākulitekṣaṇā //
2.37.d:
अपश्यच्चानुसूयात्रेः स्वप्नं भार्या पतिव्रता ।
कथयामास विप्राणां भयादाकुलितेक्षणा ॥
2.37.m:
And Anasūyā, the devoted wife of Atri, saw a dream;
with eyes agitated with fear, she told it to the brāhmaṇas:

2.37.s:
tejasā bhāsayan kṛtsnaṃ nārāyaṇasahāyavān /
bhikṣamāṇaḥ śivo nūnaṃ dṛṣṭo 'smākaṃ gṛheṣviti //
2.37.d:
तेजसा भासयन् कृत्स्नं नारायणसहायवान् ।
भिक्षमाणः शिवो नूनं दृष्टो ऽस्माकं गृहेष्विति ॥
2.37.m:
"Illuminating everything with his splendor, accompanied by Nārāyaṇa,
Śiva was surely seen begging in our houses."

2.37.s:
tasyā vacanamākarṇya śaṅkamānā maharṣayaḥ /
sarve jagmurmahāyogaṃ brahmāṇaṃ viśvasaṃbhavam //
2.37.d:
तस्या वचनमाकर्ण्य शङ्कमाना महर्षयः ।
सर्वे जग्मुर्महायोगं ब्रह्माणं विश्वसंभवम् ॥
2.37.m:
Hearing her words, the great sages, full of doubt,
all went to the great yogin Brahmā, the source of the universe,

2.37.s:
upāsyamānamamalairyogibhirbrahmavittamaiḥ /
caturvedairmūrtimadbhiḥ sāvitryā sahitaṃ prabhum //
2.37.d:
उपास्यमानममलैर्योगिभिर्ब्रह्मवित्तमैः ।
चतुर्वेदैर्मूर्तिमद्भिः सावित्र्या सहितं प्रभुम् ॥
2.37.m:
who was being worshipped by immaculate yogins, the foremost knowers of Brahman,
and by the four Vedas embodied, together with Sāvitrī, the Lord,

2.37.s:
āsīnamāsane ramye nānāścaryasamanvite /
prabhāsahasrakalile jñānaiśvaryādisaṃyute //
2.37.d:
आसीनमासने रम्ये नानाश्चर्यसमन्विते ।
प्रभासहस्रकलिले ज्ञानैश्वर्यादिसंयुते ॥
2.37.m:
seated upon a delightful throne accompanied by various wonders,
filled with a thousand splendors, endowed with knowledge, sovereign power, and the like,

2.37.s:
vibhrājamānaṃ vapuṣā sastitaṃ śubhralocanam /
caturmukhaṃ mahābāhuṃ chandomayamajaṃ param //
2.37.d:
विभ्राजमानं वपुषा सस्तितं शुभ्रलोचनम् ।
चतुर्मुखं महाबाहुं छन्दोमयमजं परम् ॥
2.37.m:
resplendent in form, smiling, with bright eyes,
four-faced, mighty-armed, composed of the meters, unborn, supreme.

2.37.s:
vilokya vedapuruṣaṃ prasannavadanaṃ śubham /
śirobhirdharaṇīṃ gatvā toṣayāmāsurīśvaram //
2.37.d:
विलोक्य वेदपुरुषं प्रसन्नवदनं शुभम् ।
शिरोभिर्धरणीं गत्वा तोषयामासुरीश्वरम् ॥
2.37.m:
Beholding the spirit of the Vedas, with a gracious face, auspicious,
they went to the earth with their heads and pleased the Lord.

2.37.s:
tān prasannamanā devaścaturmūrtiścaturmukhaḥ /
vyājahāra muniśreṣṭhāḥ kimāgamanakāraṇam //
2.37.d:
तान् प्रसन्नमना देवश्चतुर्मूर्तिश्चतुर्मुखः ।
व्याजहार मुनिश्रेष्ठाः किमागमनकारणम् ॥
2.37.m:
The four-formed, four-faced god, with a gracious mind,
spoke to them: "O best of sages, what is the reason for your coming?"

2.37.s:
tasya te vṛttamakhilaṃ brahmaṇaḥ paramātmanaḥ /
jñāpayāñcakrire sarve kṛtvā śirasi cāñjalim //
2.37.d:
तस्य ते वृत्तमखिलं ब्रह्मणः परमात्मनः ।
ज्ञापयाञ्चक्रिरे सर्वे कृत्वा शिरसि चाञ्जलिम् ॥
2.37.m:
Having placed their folded hands upon their heads, they
made known the entire event to that Brahman, the Supreme Self.

2.37.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
kaścid dāruvanaṃ puṇyaṃ puruṣo 'tīvaśobhanaḥ /
bhāryayā cārusarvāṅgyā praviṣṭo nagna eva hi //
2.37.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः
कश्चिद् दारुवनं पुण्यं पुरुषो ऽतीवशोभनः ।
भार्यया चारुसर्वाङ्ग्या प्रविष्टो नग्न एव हि ॥
2.37.m:
The sages said:
"A certain exceedingly handsome man entered the holy Dāruvana [forest]
with a wife whose limbs were all beautiful, entirely naked.

2.37.s:
mohayāmāsa vapuṣā nārīṇāṃ kulamīśvaraḥ /
kanyakānāṃ priyā cāsya dūṣayāmāsa putrakān //
2.37.d:
मोहयामास वपुषा नारीणां कुलमीश्वरः ।
कन्यकानां प्रिया चास्य दूषयामास पुत्रकान् ॥
2.37.m:
With his body, the Lord infatuated the host of women,
and his beloved corrupted the unmarried daughters and the sons.

2.37.s:
asmābhirvividhāḥ śāpāḥ pradattāśca parāhatāḥ /
tāḍito 'smābhiratyarthaṃ liṅgantu vinipātitam //
2.37.d:
अस्माभिर्विविधाः शापाः प्रदत्ताश्च पराहताः ।
ताडितो ऽस्माभिरत्यर्थं लिङ्गन्तु विनिपातितम् ॥
2.37.m:
Various curses were uttered by us, but they were repelled;
he was severely beaten by us, and his liṅga was cast down.

2.37.s:
antarhitaśca bhagavān sabhāryo liṅgameva ca /
utpātāścābhavan ghorāḥ sarvabhūtabhayaṅkarāḥ //
2.37.d:
अन्तर्हितश्च भगवान् सभार्यो लिङ्गमेव च ।
उत्पाताश्चाभवन् घोराः सर्वभूतभयङ्कराः ॥
2.37.m:
And the blessed one vanished along with his wife and the liṅga;
and terrible portents causing dread to all beings arose.

2.37.s:
ka eṣa puruṣo deva bhītāḥ sma puruṣottama /
bhavantameva śaraṇaṃ prapannā vayamacyuta //
2.37.d:
क एष पुरुषो देव भीताः स्म पुरुषोत्तम ।
भवन्तमेव शरणं प्रपन्ना वयमच्युत ॥
2.37.m:
Who was this man, O god? We are afraid, O Supreme Spirit!
We have approached you alone for refuge, O infallible one!

2.37.s:
tvaṃ hi vetsi jagatyasmin yatkiñcidapi ceṣṭitam /
anugraheṇa viśveśa tadasmānanupālaya //
2.37.d:
त्वं हि वेत्सि जगत्यस्मिन् यत्किञ्चिदपि चेष्टितम् ।
अनुग्रहेण विश्वेश तदस्माननुपालय ॥
2.37.m:
For you know whatever movement [occurs] in this world;
therefore, O lord of the universe, protect us by your grace!"

2.37.s:
vijñāpito munigaṇairviśvātmā kamalodbhavaḥ /
dhyātvā devaṃ triśūlāṅkaṃ kṛtāñjalirabhāṣata //
2.37.d:
विज्ञापितो मुनिगणैर्विश्वात्मा कमलोद्भवः ।
ध्यात्वा देवं त्रिशूलाङ्कं कृताञ्जलिरभाषत ॥
2.37.m:
Thus informed by the hosts of sages, the soul of the universe, born from a lotus,
meditated upon the god marked with the trident, and with folded hands spoke:

2.37.s:
brahmovāca
hā kaṣṭaṃ bhavatāmadya jātaṃ sarvārthanāśanam /
dhigbalaṃ dhik tapaścaryā mithyaiva bhavatāmiha //
2.37.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
हा कष्टं भवतामद्य जातं सर्वार्थनाशनम् ।
धिग्बलं धिक् तपश्चर्या मिथ्यैव भवतामिह ॥
2.37.m:
Brahmā said:
"Alas! A misfortune that destroys all purposes has befallen you today!
Fie on your strength, fie on your practice of austerities; it is completely futile for you here!

2.37.s:
saṃprāpya puṇyasaṃskārānnidhīnāṃ paramaṃ nidhim /
upekṣitaṃ vṛthācārairbhavadbhiriha mohitaiḥ //
2.37.d:
संप्राप्य पुण्यसंस्कारान्निधीनां परमं निधिम् ।
उपेक्षितं वृथाचारैर्भवद्भिरिह मोहितैः ॥
2.37.m:
Having obtained, through the impressions of merits, the supreme treasure of treasures,
it was disregarded by you here, who follow useless conduct and are deluded!

2.37.s:
kāṅkṣante yogino nityaṃ yatanto yatayo nidhim /
yameva taṃ samāsādya hā bhavadbhirupekṣitam //
2.37.d:
काङ्क्षन्ते योगिनो नित्यं यतन्तो यतयो निधिम् ।
यमेव तं समासाद्य हा भवद्भिरुपेक्षितम् ॥
2.37.m:
The treasure which yogins and striving ascetics constantly desire,
having encountered that very one, alas, it was disregarded by you!

2.37.s:
yajanti yajñairvividhairyatprāptyairvedavādinaḥ /
mahānidhiṃ samāsādya hā bhavadbhirupekṣitam //
2.37.d:
यजन्ति यज्ञैर्विविधैर्यत्प्राप्त्यैर्वेदवादिनः ।
महानिधिं समासाद्य हा भवद्भिरुपेक्षितम् ॥
2.37.m:
That for whose attainment the expounders of the Vedas sacrifice with various sacrifices,
having encountered that great treasure, alas, it was disregarded by you!

2.37.s:
yaṃ samāsādya devānaimaiśvaryamakhilaṃ jagat /
tamāsādyākṣayanidhiṃ hā bhavadbhirupekṣitam //
2.37.d:
यं समासाद्य देवानैमैश्वर्यमखिलं जगत् ।
तमासाद्याक्षयनिधिं हा भवद्भिरुपेक्षितम् ॥
2.37.m:
Attaining whom is the sovereignty of the gods, the entire universe,
having attained that imperishable treasure, alas, it was disregarded by you!

2.37.s:
yatsamāpattijanitaṃ viśveśatvamidaṃ mama /
tadevopekṣitaṃ dṛṣṭvā nidhānaṃ bhāgyavarjitaiḥ //
2.37.d:
यत्समापत्तिजनितं विश्वेशत्वमिदं मम ।
तदेवोपेक्षितं दृष्ट्वा निधानं भाग्यवर्जितैः ॥
2.37.m:
That from whose attainment this lordship of the universe of mine was born,
having seen that very treasure, it was disregarded by you who are devoid of good fortune!

2.37.s:
yasmin samāhitaṃ divyamaiśvaryaṃ yat tadavyayam /
tamāsādya nidhiṃ brāhma hā bhavadbhirvṛthākṛtam //
2.37.d:
यस्मिन् समाहितं दिव्यमैश्वर्यं यत् तदव्ययम् ।
तमासाद्य निधिं ब्राह्म हा भवद्भिर्वृथाकृतम् ॥
2.37.m:
In whom that divine, imperishable sovereignty is concentrated,
having attained that treasure of Brahman, alas, it was treated with futility by you!

2.37.s:
eṣa devo mahādevo vijñeyastu maheśvaraḥ /
na tasya paramaṃ kiñcit padaṃ samadhigamyate //
2.37.d:
एष देवो महादेवो विज्ञेयस्तु महेश्वरः ।
न तस्य परमं किञ्चित् पदं समधिगम्यते ॥
2.37.m:
This god is Mahādeva, to be known indeed as Maheśvara;
no supreme state beyond him is attained.

2.37.s:
devatānāmṛṣīṇāṃ ca pitṝṇāṃ cāpi śāśvataḥ /
sahasrayugaparyante pralaye sarvadehinām /
saṃharatyeṣa bhagavān kālo bhūtvā maheśvaraḥ //
2.37.d:
देवतानामृषीणां च पितॄणां चापि शाश्वतः ।
सहस्रयुगपर्यन्ते प्रलये सर्वदेहिनाम् ।
संहरत्येष भगवान् कालो भूत्वा महेश्वरः ॥

2.37.s:
eṣa caiva prajāḥ sarvāḥ sṛjatyekaḥ svatejasā /
eṣa cakrī ca vajrī ca śrīvatsakṛtalakṣaṇaḥ //
2.37.d:
एष चैव प्रजाः सर्वाः सृजत्येकः स्वतेजसा ।
एष चक्री च वज्री च श्रीवत्सकृतलक्षणः ॥
2.37.m:
And he alone creates all creatures by his own luster;
he bears the discus, the thunderbolt, and is marked by the Śrīvatsa.

2.37.s:
yogī kṛtayuge devastretāyāṃ yajña ucyate /
dvāpare bhagavān kālo dharmaketuḥ kalau yuge //
2.37.d:
योगी कृतयुगे देवस्त्रेतायां यज्ञ उच्यते ।
द्वापरे भगवान् कालो धर्मकेतुः कलौ युगे ॥
2.37.m:
In the Kṛta age the god is a yogin; in the Tretā age he is called the sacrifice;
in the Dvāpara age he is the blessed Time; in the Kali age he is the banner of duty.

2.37.s:
rudrasya mūrtayastistro yābhirviśvamidaṃ tatam /
tamo hyagnī rajo brahmā sattvaṃ viṣṇuriti prabhuḥ //
2.37.d:
रुद्रस्य मूर्तयस्तिस्त्रो याभिर्विश्वमिदं ततम् ।
तमो ह्यग्नी रजो ब्रह्मा सत्त्वं विष्णुरिति प्रभुः ॥
2.37.m:
Three are the forms of Rudra by which this universe is pervaded:
darkness is indeed Agni, passion is Brahmā, and goodness is Viṣṇu—thus is the Lord."

2.37.s:
mūrtiranyā smṛtā cāsya digvāsā vai śivā dhruvā /
yatra tiṣṭhati tad brahma yogena tu samanvitam //
2.37.d:
मूर्तिरन्या स्मृता चास्य दिग्वासा वै शिवा ध्रुवा ।
यत्र तिष्ठति तद् ब्रह्म योगेन तु समन्वितम् ॥
2.37.m: His other form is traditionally known as space-clad, auspicious, and eternal, / wherein rests that Brahman, joined with yoga.

2.37.s:
yā cāsya pārśvagā bhāryā bhavadbhirabhivīkṣitā /
sā hi nārāyaṇo devaḥ paramātmā sanātanaḥ //
2.37.d:
या चास्य पार्श्वगा भार्या भवद्भिरभिवीक्षिता ।
सा हि नारायणो देवः परमात्मा सनातनः ॥
2.37.m: And the wife standing at his side, whom you have seen— / she is indeed the god Nārāyaṇa, the eternal supreme self.

2.37.s:
tasmāt sarvamidaṃ jātaṃ tatraiva ca layaṃ vrajet /
sa eva mohayet kṛtsnaṃ sa eva paramā gatiḥ //
2.37.d:
तस्मात् सर्वमिदं जातं तत्रैव च लयं व्रजेत् ।
स एव मोहयेत् कृत्स्नं स एव परमा गतिः ॥
2.37.m: From him everything here arose, and into him alone it shall dissolve; / he alone deludes all, and he alone is the supreme goal.

2.37.s:
sahasraśīrṣā puruṣaḥ sahasrākṣaḥ sahasrapāt /
ekaśṛṅgo mahānātmā purāṇo 'ṣṭākṣaro hariḥ //
2.37.d:
सहस्रशीर्षा पुरुषः सहस्राक्षः सहस्रपात् ।
एकशृङ्गो महानात्मा पुराणो ऽष्टाक्षरो हरिः ॥
2.37.m: The Person of a thousand heads, a thousand eyes, and a thousand feet, / the single-horned, great self, the ancient Hari of eight syllables,

2.37.s:
caturvedaścaturmūrtistrimūrtistriguṇaḥ paraḥ /
ekamūrtirameyātmā nārāyaṇa iti śrutiḥ //
2.37.d:
चतुर्वेदश्चतुर्मूर्तिस्त्रिमूर्तिस्त्रिगुणः परः ।
एकमूर्तिरमेयात्मा नारायण इति श्रुतिः ॥
2.37.m: the four Vedas, of fourfold form, of threefold form, beyond the three qualities, / of single form, the immeasurable self—so runs the Vedic revelation: ‘Nārāyaṇa’.

2.37.s:
ṛtasya garbho bhagavānāpo māyātanuḥ prabhuḥ /
stūyate vividhairmantrairbrāhmaṇairdharmamokṣibhiḥ //
2.37.d:
ऋतस्य गर्भो भगवानापो मायातनुः प्रभुः ।
स्तूयते विविधैर्मन्त्रैर्ब्राह्मणैर्धर्ममोक्षिभिः ॥
2.37.m: The womb of cosmic order, the Blessed Lord, the waters, the master whose body is illusory creative power, / is praised with various mantras by Brahmins desiring duty and liberation.

2.37.s:
saṃhṛtya sakalaṃ viśvaṃ kalpānte puruṣottamaḥ /
śete yogāmṛtaṃ pītvā yat tad viṣṇoḥ paraṃ padam //
2.37.d:
संहृत्य सकलं विश्वं कल्पान्ते पुरुषोत्तमः ।
शेते योगामृतं पीत्वा यत् तद् विष्णोः परं पदम् ॥
2.37.m: Having withdrawn the entire universe at the end of the cosmic age, the Supreme Spirit / sleeps, having drunk the nectar of yoga, in that which is the supreme abode of Viṣṇu.

2.37.s:
na jāyate na mriyate vardhate na ca viśvasṛk /
mūlaprakṛtiravyaktā gīyate vaidikairajaḥ //
2.37.d:
न जायते न म्रियते वर्धते न च विश्वसृक् ।
मूलप्रकृतिरव्यक्ता गीयते वैदिकैरजः ॥
2.37.m: He is not born, he does not die, nor does the creator of all increase; / the unborn one is chanted by followers of the Veda as unmanifest primordial matter.

2.37.s:
tato niśāyāṃ vṛttāyāṃ sisṛkṣurakhilañjagat /
ajasya nābhau tad bījaṃ kṣipatyeṣa maheśvaraḥ //
2.37.d:
ततो निशायां वृत्तायां सिसृक्षुरखिलञ्जगत् ।
अजस्य नाभौ तद् बीजं क्षिपत्येष महेश्वरः ॥
2.37.m: Then, when the night has passed, desiring to create the entire world, / this Great Lord casts that seed into the navel of the unborn one.

2.37.s:
taṃ māṃ vitta mahātmānaṃ brahmāṇaṃ viśvato mukham /
mahāntaṃ puruṣaṃ viśvamapāṃ garbhamanuttamam //
2.37.d:
तं मां वित्त महात्मानं ब्रह्माणं विश्वतो मुखम् ।
महान्तं पुरुषं विश्वमपां गर्भमनुत्तमम् ॥
2.37.m: Know that great self to be me, Brahmā whose face is turned everywhere, / the Great Person, the universe, the womb of the waters, the unsurpassable.

2.37.s:
na taṃ vidātha janakaṃ mohitāstasya māyayā /
devadevaṃ mahādevaṃ bhūtānāmīśvaraṃ haram //
2.37.d:
न तं विदाथ जनकं मोहितास्तस्य मायया ।
देवदेवं महादेवं भूतानामीश्वरं हरम् ॥
2.37.m: Deluded by his illusory creative power, you do not know that father, / the god of gods, Mahādeva, the lord of beings, Hara.

2.37.s:
eṣa devo mahādevo hyanādirbhagavān haraḥ /
viṣṇunā saha saṃyuktaḥ karoti vikaroti ca //
2.37.d:
एष देवो महादेवो ह्यनादिर्भगवान् हरः ।
विष्णुना सह संयुक्तः करोति विकरोति च ॥
2.37.m: This god is Mahādeva, indeed the beginningless Lord Hara; / united with Viṣṇu, he creates and transforms.

2.37.s:
na tasya vidyate kāryaṃ na tasmād vidyate param /
sa vedān pradadau pūrvaṃ yogamāyātanurmama //
2.37.d:
न तस्य विद्यते कार्यं न तस्माद् विद्यते परम् ।
स वेदान् प्रददौ पूर्वं योगमायातनुर्मम ॥
2.37.m: No effect exists for him, nor does anything exist higher than him; / he, whose body is the yoga of illusory creative power, previously gave the Vedas to me.

2.37.s:
sa māyī māyayā sarvaṃ karoti vikaroti ca /
tameva muktaye jñātvā vrajeta śaraṇaṃ bhavam //
2.37.d:
स मायी मायया सर्वं करोति विकरोति च ।
तमेव मुक्तये ज्ञात्वा व्रजेत शरणं भवम् ॥
2.37.m: He, the master of illusory creative power, creates and transforms everything through that illusory power; / knowing him alone for liberation, one should take refuge in Bhava.”

2.37.s:
itīritā bhagavatā marīcipramukhā vibhum /
praṇamya devaṃ brahmāṇaṃ pṛcchanti sma suduḥ khitāḥ //
2.37.d:
इतीरिता भगवता मरीचिप्रमुखा विभुम् ।
प्रणम्य देवं ब्रह्माणं पृच्छन्ति स्म सुदुः खिताः ॥
2.37.m: Having been spoken to thus by the Blessed Lord, [the sages] headed by Marīci, bowing down / to the divine, all-pervading Brahmā, asked him in great distress.

2.37.s:
munaya ūcuḥ
kathaṃ paśyema taṃ devaṃ punareva pinākinam /
brūhi viśvāmareśāna trātā tvaṃ śaraṇaiṣiṇām //
2.37.d:
मुनय ऊचुः
कथं पश्येम तं देवं पुनरेव पिनाकिनम् ।
ब्रूहि विश्वामरेशान त्राता त्वं शरणैषिणाम् ॥
2.37.m: The sages said: / “How may we behold that god, the wielder of the Pināka, once again? / Tell us, O lord of the gods of the universe; you are the protector of those seeking refuge.”

2.37.s:
pitāmaha uvāca
yad dṛṣṭaṃ bhavatā tasya liṅgaṃ bhuvi nipātitam /
talliṅgānukṛtīśasya kṛtvā liṅgamanuttamam //
2.37.d:
पितामह उवाच
यद् दृष्टं भवता तस्य लिङ्गं भुवि निपातितम् ।
तल्लिङ्गानुकृतीशस्य कृत्वा लिङ्गमनुत्तमम् ॥
2.37.m: The Grandfather said: / “Since you saw his liṅga cast down upon the earth, / make an unsurpassable liṅga imitating that liṅga of the Lord,

2.37.s:
pūjayadhvaṃ sapatnīkāḥ sādaraṃ putrasaṃyutāḥ /
vaidikaireva niyamairvividhairbrahmacāriṇaḥ //
2.37.d:
पूजयध्वं सपत्नीकाः सादरं पुत्रसंयुताः ।
वैदिकैरेव नियमैर्विविधैर्ब्रह्मचारिणः ॥
2.37.m: and worship it with reverence together with your wives and accompanied by your sons, / practicing celibacy according to Vedic observances alone.

2.37.s:
saṃsthāpya śāṅkarairmantrairṛgyajuḥ sāmasaṃbhavaiḥ /
tapaḥ paraṃ samāsthāya gṛṇantaḥ śatarudriyam //
2.37.d:
संस्थाप्य शाङ्करैर्मन्त्रैरृग्यजुः सामसंभवैः ।
तपः परं समास्थाय गृणन्तः शतरुद्रियम् ॥
2.37.m: Having consecrated it with mantras belonging to Śaṅkara, originating from the Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāma Vedas, / undertaking supreme asceticism and chanting the Śatarudriya,

2.37.s:
samāhitāḥ pūjayadhvaṃ saputrāḥ saha bandhubhiḥ /
sarve prāñjalayo bhūtvā śūlapāṇiṃ prapadyatha //
2.37.d:
समाहिताः पूजयध्वं सपुत्राः सह बन्धुभिः ।
सर्वे प्राञ्जलयो भूत्वा शूलपाणिं प्रपद्यथ ॥
2.37.m: focused in mind, worship it together with your sons and alongside your kinsmen; / all of you, with hands folded in reverence, take refuge in the wielder of the trident.

2.37.s:
tato drakṣyatha deveśaṃ durdarśamakṛtātmabhiḥ /
yaṃ dṛṣṭvā sarvamajñānamadharmaśca praṇaśyati //
2.37.d:
ततो द्रक्ष्यथ देवेशं दुर्दर्शमकृतात्मभिः ।
यं दृष्ट्वा सर्वमज्ञानमधर्मश्च प्रणश्यति ॥
2.37.m: Then you will behold the Lord of gods, difficult to be seen by those who have not purified themselves, / seeing whom all ignorance and unrighteousness perish.”

2.37.s:
tataḥ praṇamya varadaṃ brahmāṇamamitaujasam /
jagmuḥ saṃhṛṣṭamanaso devadāruvanaṃ punaḥ //
2.37.d:
ततः प्रणम्य वरदं ब्रह्माणममितौजसम् ।
जग्मुः संहृष्टमनसो देवदारुवनं पुनः ॥
2.37.m: Then, having bowed to Brahmā of boundless majesty, the granter of boons, / with delighted minds they went back to the Devadāru forest.

2.37.s:
ārādhayitumārabdhā brahmaṇā kathitaṃ yathā /
ajānantaḥ paraṃ devaṃ vītarāgā vimatsarāḥ //
2.37.d:
आराधयितुमारब्धा ब्रह्मणा कथितं यथा ।
अजानन्तः परं देवं वीतरागा विमत्सराः ॥
2.37.m: Free from passion and free from malice, they began to worship / as told by Brahmā, not knowing the supreme god:

2.37.s:
sthaṇḍileṣu vicitreṣu parvatānāṃ guhāsu ca /
nadīnāṃ ca vivikteṣu pulineṣu śubheṣu ca //
2.37.d:
स्थण्डिलेषु विचित्रेषु पर्वतानां गुहासु च ।
नदीनां च विविक्तेषु पुलिनेषु शुभेषु च ॥
2.37.m: on bare sacrificial grounds, in the caves of mountains, / and on the auspicious, secluded sandy banks of rivers,

2.37.s:
śaivālabhojanāḥ kecit kecidantarjaleśayāḥ /
kecidabhrāvakāśāstu pādāṅguṣṭhāgraviṣṭhitāḥ //
2.37.d:
शैवालभोजनाः केचित् केचिदन्तर्जलेशयाः ।
केचिदभ्रावकाशास्तु पादाङ्गुष्ठाग्रविष्ठिताः ॥
2.37.m: some feeding on moss, some lying inside water, / some exposed to the sky, standing on the tips of their big toes,

2.37.s:
danto 'lūkhalinastvanye hyaśmakuṭṭāstathā pare /
śākaparṇāśinaḥ kecit saṃprakṣālā marīcipāḥ //
2.37.d:
दन्तो ऽलूखलिनस्त्वन्ये ह्यश्मकुट्टास्तथा परे ।
शाकपर्णाशिनः केचित् संप्रक्षाला मरीचिपाः ॥
2.37.m: others using their teeth as a mortar, others grinding with stones, / some eating greens and leaves, some washing their pots after each meal, some drinking sunbeams,

2.37.s:
vṛkṣamūlaniketāśca śilāśayyāstathā pare /
kālaṃ nayanti tapasā pūjayanto maheśvaram //
2.37.d:
वृक्षमूलनिकेताश्च शिलाशय्यास्तथा परे ।
कालं नयन्ति तपसा पूजयन्तो महेश्वरम् ॥
2.37.m: others having their abode at the roots of trees, and others sleeping on rock beds, / they spend their time in asceticism, worshipping the Great Lord.

2.37.s:
tatasteṣāṃ prasādārthaṃ prapannārtiharo haraḥ /
cakā bhagavān buddhiṃ prabodhāya vṛṣadhvajaḥ //
2.37.d:
ततस्तेषां प्रसादार्थं प्रपन्नार्तिहरो हरः ।
चका भगवान् बुद्धिं प्रबोधाय वृषध्वजः ॥
2.37.m: Then, to show favor to them, Hara, who removes the distress of the surrendered, / the Blessed Lord, whose emblem is the bull, made up his mind to enlighten them.

2.37.s:
devaḥ kṛtayuge hyasmin śṛṅge himavataḥ śubhe /
devadāruvanaṃ prāptaḥ prasannaḥ parameśvaraḥ //
2.37.d:
देवः कृतयुगे ह्यस्मिन् शृङ्गे हिमवतः शुभे ।
देवदारुवनं प्राप्तः प्रसन्नः परमेश्वरः ॥
2.37.m: In this Kṛtayuga, the god, the Supreme Lord, becoming pleased, / arrived at the Devadāru forest on an auspicious peak of the Himālaya.

2.37.s:
bhasmapāṇḍuradigdhāṅgo nagno vikṛtalakṣaṇaḥ /
ulmukavyagrahastaśca raktapiṅgalalocanaḥ //
2.37.d:
भस्मपाण्डुरदिग्धाङ्गो नग्नो विकृतलक्षणः ।
उल्मुकव्यग्रहस्तश्च रक्तपिङ्गललोचनः ॥
2.37.m: His limbs were smeared white with ashes; he was naked, deformed in appearance, / holding a burning firebrand in his restless hand, with eyes reddish-brown.

2.37.s:
kvacicca hasate raudraṃ kvacid gāyati vismitaḥ /
kvacinnṛtyati śṛṅgārī kvacidrauti muhurmuhuḥ //
2.37.d:
क्वचिच्च हसते रौद्रं क्वचिद् गायति विस्मितः ।
क्वचिन्नृत्यति शृङ्गारी क्वचिद्रौति मुहुर्मुहुः ॥
2.37.m: In one place he laughs terribly, in another he sings as if amazed; / in one place he dances amorously, in another he cries out repeatedly.

2.37.s:
āśrame 'bhyāgato bhikṣāṃ yācate ca punaḥ punaḥ /
māyāṃ kṛtvātmano rūpaṃ devastad vanamāgataḥ //
2.37.d:
आश्रमे ऽभ्यागतो भिक्षां याचते च पुनः पुनः ।
मायां कृत्वात्मनो रूपं देवस्तद् वनमागतः ॥
2.37.m: Having arrived at the hermitage, he begs for alms again and again; / assuming a form made of his own illusory creative power, the god entered that forest,

2.37.s:
kṛtvā girisutāṃ gaurīṃ pārśvedevaḥ pinākadhṛk /
sā ca pūrvavad deveśī devadāruvanaṃ gatā //
2.37.d:
कृत्वा गिरिसुतां गौरीं पार्श्वेदेवः पिनाकधृक् ।
सा च पूर्ववद् देवेशी देवदारुवनं गता ॥
2.37.m: having placed Gaurī, the daughter of the mountain, at his side, the god wielding the Pināka. / And she, the ruler of gods, went to the Devadāru forest as before.

2.37.s:
dṛṣṭvā samāgataṃ devaṃ devyā saha kapardinam /
praṇemuḥ śirasā bhūmau toṣayāmāsurīśvaram //
2.37.d:
दृष्ट्वा समागतं देवं देव्या सह कपर्दिनम् ।
प्रणेमुः शिरसा भूमौ तोषयामासुरीश्वरम् ॥
2.37.m: Seeing that the matted-haired god had arrived along with the goddess, / they bowed down with their heads to the ground and propitiated the Lord

2.37.s:
vaidikairvividhairmantraiḥ sūktairmāheśvaraiḥ śubhaiḥ /
atharvaśirasā cānye rudrādyairbrahmabhirbhavam //
2.37.d:
वैदिकैर्विविधैर्मन्त्रैः सूक्तैर्माहेश्वरैः शुभैः ।
अथर्वशिरसा चान्ये रुद्राद्यैर्ब्रह्मभिर्भवम् ॥
2.37.m: with various Vedic mantras and auspicious hymns to the Great Lord, / and others [propitiated] Bhava with the Atharvaśiras and with sacred texts such as the Rudra:

2.37.s:
namo devādidevāya mahādevāya te namaḥ /
tryambakāya namastubhyaṃ triśūlavaradhāriṇe //
2.37.d:
नमो देवादिदेवाय महादेवाय ते नमः ।
त्र्यम्बकाय नमस्तुभ्यं त्रिशूलवरधारिणे ॥
2.37.m: “Obeisance to you, the supreme god of gods, Mahādeva, obeisance to you, / to Tryambaka, obeisance to you, the bearer of the excellent trident.

2.37.s:
namo digvāsase tubhyaṃ vikṛtāya pinākine /
sarvapraṇatadehāya svayamapraṇatātmane //
2.37.d:
नमो दिग्वाससे तुभ्यं विकृताय पिनाकिने ।
सर्वप्रणतदेहाय स्वयमप्रणतात्मने ॥
2.37.m: Obeisance to you, the space-clad, the deformed one, the wielder of the Pināka, / to whom all bodies bow, yet who himself bows to none.

2.37.s:
antakāntakṛte tubhyaṃ sarvasaṃharaṇāya ca /
namo 'stu nṛtyaśīlāya namo bhairavarūpiṇe //
2.37.d:
अन्तकान्तकृते तुभ्यं सर्वसंहरणाय च ।
नमो ऽस्तु नृत्यशीलाय नमो भैरवरूपिणे ॥
2.37.m: To you, the ender of Death, and the destroyer of all, / obeisance be to you whose nature is dancing, obeisance to you whose form is Bhairava.

2.37.s:
naranārīśarīrāya yogināṃ gurave namaḥ /
namo dāntāya śāntāya tāpasāya harāya ca //
2.37.d:
नरनारीशरीराय योगिनां गुरवे नमः ।
नमो दान्ताय शान्ताय तापसाय हराय च ॥
2.37.m: To the one whose body is man and woman, to the teacher of yogins, obeisance; / obeisance to the self-controlled, the tranquil, the ascetic, and to Hara.

2.37.s:
vibhīṣaṇāya rudrāya namaste kṛttivāsase /
namaste lelihānāya śitikaṇṭhāya te namaḥ //
2.37.d:
विभीषणाय रुद्राय नमस्ते कृत्तिवाससे ।
नमस्ते लेलिहानाय शितिकण्ठाय ते नमः ॥
2.37.m: To the terrifying Rudra, obeisance to you who are clad in animal skins; / obeisance to you, the licking one, to the blue-throated one, obeisance to you.

2.37.s:
aghoraghorarūpāya vāmadevāya vai namaḥ /
namaḥ kanakamālāya devyāḥ priyakarāya ca //
2.37.d:
अघोरघोररूपाय वामदेवाय वै नमः ।
नमः कनकमालाय देव्याः प्रियकराय च ॥
2.37.m: To Vāmadeva whose form is both non-terrific and terrific, obeisance; / obeisance to the golden-garlanded one, the one who brings joy to the goddess.

2.37.s:
gaṅgāsaliladhārāya śambhave parameṣṭhine /
namo yogādhipataye brahmādhipataye namaḥ //
2.37.d:
गङ्गासलिलधाराय शम्भवे परमेष्ठिने ।
नमो योगाधिपतये ब्रह्माधिपतये नमः ॥
2.37.m: To the bearer of the waters of the Gaṅgā, to Śambhu, the supreme ruler, / obeisance to the sovereign of yoga, obeisance to the sovereign of Brahman.”

2.37.s:
prāṇāya ca namastubhyaṃ namo bhasmāṅgarāgine /
namaste ghanavāhāya daṃṣṭriṇe vahniretase //
2.37.d:
प्राणाय च नमस्तुभ्यं नमो भस्माङ्गरागिने ।
नमस्ते घनवाहाय दंष्ट्रिणे वह्निरेतसे ॥
2.37.m: Salutation to you, the vital breath! Salutation to the one whose limbs are smeared with ashes! / Salutation to you whose vehicle is the cloud, the fanged one, whose seed is fire!

2.37.s:
brahmaṇaśca śiro hartre namaste kālarūpiṇe /
āgatiṃ te na janīmo gatiṃ naiva ca naiva ca /
viśveśvara mahādeva yo 'si so 'si namo 'stu te //
2.37.d:
ब्रह्मणश्च शिरो हर्त्रे नमस्ते कालरूपिणे ।
आगतिं ते न जनीमो गतिं नैव च नैव च ।
विश्वेश्वर महादेव यो ऽसि सो ऽसि नमो ऽस्तु ते ॥
2.37.m: Salutation to you who removed Brahmā's head, the one whose form is Time! / We do not know your arrival, nor do we know your departure at all. / O Lord of the universe, O Mahādeva, whoever you are, salutation be to you!

2.37.s:
namaḥ pramathanāthāya dātre ca śubhasaṃpadām /
kapālapāṇaye tubhyaṃ namo mīḍhuṣṭamāya te /
namaḥ kanakaliṅgāya vāriliṅgāya te namaḥ //
2.37.d:
नमः प्रमथनाथाय दात्रे च शुभसंपदाम् ।
कपालपाणये तुभ्यं नमो मीढुष्टमाय ते ।
नमः कनकलिङ्गाय वारिलिङ्गाय ते नमः ॥
2.37.m: Salutation to the lord of the Pramathas, the bestower of auspicious fortunes! / To you who hold a skull in your hand, salutation to you, the most bountiful! / Salutation to the golden liṅga! Salutation to you, the water-liṅga!

2.37.s:
namo vahnyarkaliṅgāya jñānaliṅgāya te namaḥ /
namo bhujaṅgahārāya karṇikārapriyāya ca /
kirīṭine kuṇḍaline kālakālāya te namaḥ //
2.37.d:
नमो वह्न्यर्कलिङ्गाय ज्ञानलिङ्गाय ते नमः ।
नमो भुजङ्गहाराय कर्णिकारप्रियाय च ।
किरीटिने कुण्डलिने कालकालाय ते नमः ॥
2.37.m: Salutation to the fire-and-sun-liṅga! Salutation to you, the knowledge-liṅga! / Salutation to the one with a garland of serpents, fond of the Karṇikāra blossom, / crowned with a diadem, wearing earrings; salutation to you, the death of Death!

2.37.s:
vāmadeva maheśāna devadeva trilocana /
kṣamyatāṃ yatkṛtaṃ mohāt tvameva śaraṇaṃ hi naḥ //
2.37.d:
वामदेव महेशान देवदेव त्रिलोचन ।
क्षम्यतां यत्कृतं मोहात् त्वमेव शरणं हि नः ॥
2.37.m: O Vāmadeva, O Great Lord, O God of gods, O three-eyed one, / may whatever was done out of delusion be forgiven, for you alone are our refuge!

2.37.s:
caritāni vicitrāṇi guhyāni gahanāni ca /
brahmādīnāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ durvijñeyo 'si śaṅkara //
2.37.d:
चरितानि विचित्राणि गुह्यानि गहनानि च ।
ब्रह्मादीनां च सर्वेषां दुर्विज्ञेयो ऽसि शङ्कर ॥
2.37.m: Your deeds are manifold, secret, and unfathomable; / and you are difficult to comprehend even for all [the gods] headed by Brahmā, O Śaṅkara!

2.37.s:
ajñānād yadi vā jñānād yatkiñcitkurute naraḥ /
tatsarvaṃ bhagavānena kurute yogamāyayā //
2.37.d:
अज्ञानाद् यदि वा ज्ञानाद् यत्किञ्चित्कुरुते नरः ।
तत्सर्वं भगवानेन कुरुते योगमायया ॥
2.37.m: Whatever a person does, whether out of ignorance or knowledge, / the Lord does all that through him by his illusory yogic power.

2.37.s:
evaṃ stutvā mahādevaṃ prahṛṣṭenāntarātmanā /
ūcuḥ praṇamya giriśaṃ paśyāmastvāṃ yathā purā //
2.37.d:
एवं स्तुत्वा महादेवं प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना ।
ऊचुः प्रणम्य गिरिशं पश्यामस्त्वां यथा पुरा ॥
2.37.m: Having thus praised Mahādeva with delighted inner selves, / bowing to the mountain-dweller, they said: 'May we see you as you were before.'

2.37.s:
teṣāṃ saṃstavamākarṇya somaḥ momavibhūṣaṇaḥ /
svameva paramaṃ rūpaṃ darśayāmāsa śaṅkaraḥ //
2.37.d:
तेषां संस्तवमाकर्ण्य सोमः मोमविभूषणः ।
स्वमेव परमं रूपं दर्शयामास शङ्करः ॥
2.37.m: Hearing their hymn of praise, Śaṅkara, united with Umā and adorned with the moon, / displayed his own supreme form.

2.37.s:
taṃ te dṛṣṭvātha giriśaṃ devyā saha pinākinam /
yathā pūrvaṃ sthitā viprāḥ praṇemurhṛṣṭamānasāḥ //
2.37.d:
तं ते दृष्ट्वाथ गिरिशं देव्या सह पिनाकिनम् ।
यथा पूर्वं स्थिता विप्राः प्रणेमुर्हृष्टमानसाः ॥
2.37.m: Then, having seen that mountain-dweller, the wielder of the Pināka, together with the Goddess, / the brāhmaṇas, standing as before, bowed down with gladdened hearts.

2.37.s:
tataste munayaḥ sarve saṃstūya ca maheśvaram /
bhṛgvaṅgirovasiṣṭhāstu viśvāmitrastathaiva ca //
2.37.d:
ततस्ते मुनयः सर्वे संस्तूय च महेश्वरम् ।
भृग्वङ्गिरोवसिष्ठास्तु विश्वामित्रस्तथैव च ॥
2.37.m: Then all those sages, having praised the Great Lord— / Bhṛgu, Aṅgiras, and Vasiṣṭha, as well as Viśvāmitra,

2.37.s:
gautamo 'triḥ sukeśaśca pulastyaḥ pulahaḥ kratuḥ /
marīciḥ kaśyapaścāpi saṃvartaśca mahātapāḥ /
praṇamya devadeveśamidaṃ vacanamabruvan //
2.37.d:
गौतमो ऽत्रिः सुकेशश्च पुलस्त्यः पुलहः क्रतुः ।
मरीचिः कश्यपश्चापि संवर्तश्च महातपाः ।
प्रणम्य देवदेवेशमिदं वचनमब्रुवन् ॥
2.37.m: Gautama, Atri, Sukeśa, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, / Marīci, Kaśyapa, and the strictly ascetic Saṃvarta— / having bowed to the Lord of the God of gods, spoke these words:

2.37.s:
kathaṃ tvāṃ devadeveśa karmayogena vā prabho /
jñānena vātha yogena pūjayāmaḥ sadaiva hi //
2.37.d:
कथं त्वां देवदेवेश कर्मयोगेन वा प्रभो ।
ज्ञानेन वाथ योगेन पूजयामः सदैव हि ॥
2.37.m: 'How, O Lord of the God of gods, O master, should we constantly worship you— / through the yoga of action, or through knowledge, or through yoga?

2.37.s:
kena vā devamārgeṇa saṃpūjyo bhagavāniha /
kiṃ tat sevyamasevyaṃ vā sarvametad bravīhi naḥ //
2.37.d:
केन वा देवमार्गेण संपूज्यो भगवानिह ।
किं तत् सेव्यमसेव्यं वा सर्वमेतद् ब्रवीहि नः ॥
2.37.m: Or by what divine path is the Lord to be worshipped here? / What is to be practiced or not to be practiced? Tell us all of this!'

2.37.s:
devadeva uvāca
etad vaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi gūḍhaṃ gahanamuttamam /
brahmaṇe kathitaṃ pūrvamādāveva maharṣayaḥ //
2.37.d:
देवदेव उवाच
एतद् वः संप्रवक्ष्यामि गूढं गहनमुत्तमम् ।
ब्रह्मणे कथितं पूर्वमादावेव महर्षयः ॥
2.37.m: The God of gods said: / 'I shall explain this to you, the secret, deep, and supreme [path] / which was told of old to Brahmā at the very beginning, O great sages.

2.37.s:
sāṃkhyayogo dvidhā jñeyaḥ puruṣāṇāṃ hi sādhanam /
yogena sahitaṃ sāṃkhyaṃ puruṣāṇāṃ vimuktidam //
2.37.d:
सांख्ययोगो द्विधा ज्ञेयः पुरुषाणां हि साधनम् ।
योगेन सहितं सांख्यं पुरुषाणां विमुक्तिदम् ॥
2.37.m: Sāṃkhya and Yoga are to be known as two kinds of spiritual practice for men; / Sāṃkhya combined with Yoga bestows liberation upon men.

2.37.s:
na kevalena yogena dṛśyate puruṣaḥ paraḥ /
jñānaṃ tu kevalaṃ samyagapavargaphalapradam //
2.37.d:
न केवलेन योगेन दृश्यते पुरुषः परः ।
ज्ञानं तु केवलं सम्यगपवर्गफलप्रदम् ॥
2.37.m: The supreme spirit is not seen by Yoga alone; / but pure knowledge completely bestows the fruit of liberation.

2.37.s:
bhavantaḥ kevalaṃ yogaṃ samāśritya vimuktaye /
vihāya sāṃkhyaṃ vimalamakurvanta pariśramam //
2.37.d:
भवन्तः केवलं योगं समाश्रित्य विमुक्तये ।
विहाय सांख्यं विमलमकुर्वन्त परिश्रमम् ॥
2.37.m: Taking recourse to Yoga alone for the sake of liberation / and abandoning pure Sāṃkhya, you underwent fruitless toil.

2.37.s:
etasmāt kāraṇād viprānṛṇāṃ kevaladharmiṇām /
āgato 'hamimaṃ deśaṃ jñāpayan mohasaṃbhavam //
2.37.d:
एतस्मात् कारणाद् विप्रानृणां केवलधर्मिणाम् ।
आगतो ऽहमिमं देशं ज्ञापयन् मोहसंभवम् ॥
2.37.m: For this reason, O brāhmaṇas, I came to this region / to instruct men devoted solely to ritual about the delusion that has arisen.

2.37.s:
tasmād bhavadbhirvimalaṃ jñānaṃ kaivalyasādhanam /
jñātavyaṃ hi prayatnena śrotavyaṃ dṛśyameva ca //
2.37.d:
तस्माद् भवद्भिर्विमलं ज्ञानं कैवल्यसाधनम् ।
ज्ञातव्यं हि प्रयत्नेन श्रोतव्यं दृश्यमेव च ॥
2.37.m: Therefore, the pure knowledge that accomplishes absolute isolation / must be known with effort by you, heard, and indeed seen.

2.37.s:
ekaḥ sarvatrago hyātmā kevalaścitimātrakaḥ /
ānando nirmalo nityaṃ syādetat sāṃkhyadarśanam //
2.37.d:
एकः सर्वत्रगो ह्यात्मा केवलश्चितिमात्रकः ।
आनन्दो निर्मलो नित्यं स्यादेतत् सांख्यदर्शनम् ॥
2.37.m: The self is one, all-pervading, solitary, pure consciousness, / bliss, and eternally immaculate: this is the view of Sāṃkhya.

2.37.s:
etadeva paraṃ jñānameṣa mokṣo 'tra gīyate /
etat kaivalyamamalaṃ brahmabhāvaśca varṇitaḥ //
2.37.d:
एतदेव परं ज्ञानमेष मोक्षो ऽत्र गीयते ।
एतत् कैवल्यममलं ब्रह्मभावश्च वर्णितः ॥
2.37.m: This alone is the supreme knowledge; this is proclaimed here as liberation; / this is described as spotless absolute isolation and the state of Brahman.

2.37.s:
āśritya caitat paramaṃ tanniṣṭhāstatparāyaṇāḥ /
paśyanti māṃ mahātmāno yatayo viśvamīśvaram //
2.37.d:
आश्रित्य चैतत् परमं तन्निष्ठास्तत्परायणाः ।
पश्यन्ति मां महात्मानो यतयो विश्वमीश्वरम् ॥
2.37.m: Taking refuge in this supreme [knowledge], established in it, and intent upon it, / the great-souled ascetics behold me, the universal Lord.

2.37.s:
etat tat paramaṃ jñānaṃ kevalaṃ sannirañjanam /
ahaṃ hi vedyo bhagavān mama mūrtiriyaṃ śivā //
2.37.d:
एतत् तत् परमं ज्ञानं केवलं सन्निरञ्जनम् ।
अहं हि वेद्यो भगवान् मम मूर्तिरियं शिवा ॥
2.37.m: This is that supreme knowledge, solitary, existing, and stainless; / I, the Lord, am to be known; this auspicious form is mine.

2.37.s:
bahūni sādhanānīha siddhaye kathitāni tu /
teṣāmabhyadhikaṃ jñānaṃ māmakaṃ dvijapuṅgavāḥ //
2.37.d:
बहूनि साधनानीह सिद्धये कथितानि तु ।
तेषामभ्यधिकं ज्ञानं मामकं द्विजपुङ्गवाः ॥
2.37.m: Many means have been taught here for attainment, / but superior to them is my knowledge, O best of the twice-born.

2.37.s:
jñānayogaratāḥ śāntā māmeva śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ /
ye hi māṃ bhasmaniratā dhyāyanti satataṃ hṛdi //
2.37.d:
ज्ञानयोगरताः शान्ता मामेव शरणं गताः ।
ये हि मां भस्मनिरता ध्यायन्ति सततं हृदि ॥
2.37.m: Devoted to the yoga of knowledge, peaceful, taking refuge in me alone, / those who, devoted to sacred ash, constantly meditate on me in their heart,

2.37.s:
madbhaktiparamā nityaṃ yatayaḥ kṣīṇakalmaṣāḥ /
nāśayāmyacirāt teṣāṃ ghoraṃ saṃsārasāgaram //
2.37.d:
मद्भक्तिपरमा नित्यं यतयः क्षीणकल्मषाः ।
नाशयाम्यचिरात् तेषां घोरं संसारसागरम् ॥
2.37.m: ever intent upon devotion to me, ascetics whose sins have been destroyed— / I swiftly destroy for them the terrible ocean of cyclic existence.

2.37.s:
praśāntaḥ saṃyatamanā bhasmoddhūlitavigrahaḥ /
brahmacaryarato nagno vrataṃ pāśupataṃ caret //
2.37.d:
प्रशान्तः संयतमना भस्मोद्धूलितविग्रहः ।
ब्रह्मचर्यरतो नग्नो व्रतं पाशुपतं चरेत् ॥
2.37.m: Tranquil, with restrained mind, his body dusted with ashes, / devoted to celibacy, naked, one should observe the Pāśupata vow.

2.37.s:
nirmitaṃ hi mayā pūrvaṃ vrataṃ pāśupataṃ param /
guhyād guhyatamaṃ sūkṣmaṃ vedasāraṃ vimuktaye //
2.37.d:
निर्मितं हि मया पूर्वं व्रतं पाशुपतं परम् ।
गुह्याद् गुह्यतमं सूक्ष्मं वेदसारं विमुक्तये ॥
2.37.m: For this supreme Pāśupata vow was fashioned by me of old, / most secret of secrets, subtle, the essence of the Veda, leading to liberation.

2.37.s:
yad vā kaupīnavasanaḥ syād vaikavasano muniḥ /
vedābhyāsarato vidvān dhyāyet paśupatiṃ śivam //
2.37.d:
यद् वा कौपीनवसनः स्याद् वैकवसनो मुनिः ।
वेदाभ्यासरतो विद्वान् ध्यायेत् पशुपतिं शिवम् ॥
2.37.m: Or else the sage may wear a loincloth, or wear a single garment; / devoted to Vedic study and learned, he should meditate on Śiva, the Lord of beasts.

2.37.s:
eṣa pāśupato yogaḥ sevanīyo mumukṣubhiḥ /
bhasmacchannairhi satataṃ niṣkāmairiti viśrutiḥ //
2.37.d:
एष पाशुपतो योगः सेवनीयो मुमुक्षुभिः ।
भस्मच्छन्नैर्हि सततं निष्कामैरिति विश्रुतिः ॥
2.37.m: This is the Pāśupata Yoga to be cultivated by seekers of liberation, / constantly covered in ashes and free from desire; so it is renowned.

2.37.s:
vītarāgabhayakrodhā manmayā māmupāśritāḥ /
bahavo 'nena yogena pūtā madbhāvamāgatāḥ //
2.37.d:
वीतरागभयक्रोधा मन्मया मामुपाश्रिताः ।
बहवो ऽनेन योगेन पूता मद्भावमागताः ॥
2.37.m: Free from attachment, fear, and anger, absorbed in me, taking refuge in me, / purified by this yoga, many have attained my being.

2.37.s:
anyāni caiva śāstrāṇi loke 'smin mohanānitu /
vedavādaviruddhāni mayaiva kathitāni tu //
2.37.d:
अन्यानि चैव शास्त्राणि लोके ऽस्मिन् मोहनानितु ।
वेदवादविरुद्धानि मयैव कथितानि तु ॥
2.37.m: And the other scriptures in this world that cause delusion / and contradict the Vedic doctrine were also proclaimed by me alone.

2.37.s:
vāmaṃ pāśupataṃ somaṃ lākulaṃ caiva bhairavam /
asevyametat kathitaṃ vedavāhyaṃ tathetaram //
2.37.d:
वामं पाशुपतं सोमं लाकुलं चैव भैरवम् ।
असेव्यमेतत् कथितं वेदवाह्यं तथेतरम् ॥
2.37.m: The Vāma, the Pāśupata, the Soma, the Lākula, and the Bhairava— / these are declared not to be practiced, being outside the Veda, and similarly other such [systems].

2.37.s:
vedamurtirahaṃ viprā nānyaśāstrārthavedibhiḥ /
jñāyate matsvarūpaṃ tu muktvā vedaṃ sanātanam //
2.37.d:
वेदमुर्तिरहं विप्रा नान्यशास्त्रार्थवेदिभिः ।
ज्ञायते मत्स्वरूपं तु मुक्त्वा वेदं सनातनम् ॥
2.37.m: I am the embodiment of the Veda, O brāhmaṇas; my essential nature / is not known by those who understand the meaning of other scriptures, setting aside the eternal Veda.

2.37.s:
sthāpayadhvamidaṃ mārgaṃ pūjayadhvaṃ maheśvaram /
acirādaiśvaraṃ jñānamutpatsyati na saṃśayaḥ //
2.37.d:
स्थापयध्वमिदं मार्गं पूजयध्वं महेश्वरम् ।
अचिरादैश्वरं ज्ञानमुत्पत्स्यति न संशयः ॥
2.37.m: Establish this path and worship the Great Lord; / divine knowledge will arise without delay, there is no doubt.

2.37.s:
mayi bhaktiśca vipulā bhavatāmastu sattamāḥ /
dhyātamātro hi sānnidhyaṃ dāsyāmi munisattamāḥ //
2.37.d:
मयि भक्तिश्च विपुला भवतामस्तु सत्तमाः ।
ध्यातमात्रो हि सान्निध्यं दास्यामि मुनिसत्तमाः ॥
2.37.m: And may you have immense devotion to me, O best of men; / as soon as I am meditated upon, I will grant my presence, O best of sages.'

2.37.s:
ityuktvā bhagavān somastatraivāntaradhīyata /
to 'pi dāruvane tasmin pūjayanti sma śaṅkaram /
brahmacaryaratāḥ śāntā jñānayogaparāyaṇāḥ //
2.37.d:
इत्युक्त्वा भगवान् सोमस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत ।
तो ऽपि दारुवने तस्मिन् पूजयन्ति स्म शङ्करम् ।
ब्रह्मचर्यरताः शान्ता ज्ञानयोगपरायणाः ॥
2.37.m: Having spoken thus, the Lord Soma vanished right there; / and they too worshipped Śaṅkara in that Dāru forest, / devoted to celibacy, peaceful, intent on the yoga of knowledge.

2.37.s:
sametya te mahātmāno munayo brahmavādinaḥ /
vitenire bahūn vādānnadhyātmajñānasaṃśrayān //
2.37.d:
समेत्य ते महात्मानो मुनयो ब्रह्मवादिनः ।
वितेनिरे बहून् वादान्नध्यात्मज्ञानसंश्रयान् ॥
2.37.m: Meeting together, those great-souled sages, knowers of Brahman, / conducted many debates concerning knowledge of the self:

2.37.s:
kimasya jagato mūlamātmā cāsmākameva hi /
ko 'pi syāt sarvabhāvānāṃ heturīśvara eva ca //
2.37.d:
किमस्य जगतो मूलमात्मा चास्माकमेव हि ।
को ऽपि स्यात् सर्वभावानां हेतुरीश्वर एव च ॥
2.37.m: 'What is the root of this universe, and what indeed is our own self? / What could be the cause of all existents, and who is the Lord?'

2.37.s:
ityevaṃ manyamānānāṃ dhyānamārgāvalambinām /
āvirāsīnmahādevī devī girivarātmajā //
2.37.d:
इत्येवं मन्यमानानां ध्यानमार्गावलम्बिनाम् ।
आविरासीन्महादेवी देवी गिरिवरात्मजा ॥
2.37.m: While they were reflecting in this manner, relying on the path of meditation, / the Great Goddess appeared, the Goddess, daughter of the best of mountains,

2.37.s:
koṭisūryapratīkāśā jvālāmālāsamāvṛtā /
svabhābhirvimalābhistu pūrayantī nabhastalam //
2.37.d:
कोटिसूर्यप्रतीकाशा ज्वालामालासमावृता ।
स्वभाभिर्विमलाभिस्तु पूरयन्ती नभस्तलम् ॥
2.37.m: resembling ten million suns, surrounded by garlands of flames, / filling the vault of the sky with her immaculate radiances.

2.37.s:
tāmanvapaśyan girijāmameyāṃ
jvālāsahasrāntarasanniviṣṭām /
praṇemurekāmakhileśapatnīṃ
jānanti te tat paramasya bījam //
2.37.d:
तामन्वपश्यन् गिरिजाममेयां
ज्वालासहस्रान्तरसन्निविष्टाम् ।
प्रणेमुरेकामखिलेशपत्नीं
जानन्ति ते तत् परमस्य बीजम् ॥
2.37.m: They beheld that immeasurable mountain-born Goddess, / stationed in the midst of thousands of flames; / they bowed down to the sole consort of the Lord of all, / knowing her to be the seed of the Supreme.

2.37.s:
asamākameṣā parameśapatnī
gatistathātmā gaganābhidhānā /
paśyantyathātmānamidaṃ ca kṛtsnaṃ
tasyāmathaite munayaśca viprāḥ //
2.37.d:
असमाकमेषा परमेशपत्नी
गतिस्तथात्मा गगनाभिधाना ।
पश्यन्त्यथात्मानमिदं च कृत्स्नं
तस्यामथैते मुनयश्च विप्राः ॥
2.37.m: This consort of the Supreme Lord, who is termed the sky, / is our refuge and our self; / and then these sages, these brāhmaṇas, / beheld themselves and this whole [universe] within her.

2.37.s:
nirīkṣitāste parameśapatnyā
tadantare devamaśeṣahetum /
paśyanti śaṃbhuṃ kavimīśitāraṃ
rudraṃ bṛhantaṃ puruṣaṃ purāṇam //
2.37.d:
निरीक्षितास्ते परमेशपत्न्या
तदन्तरे देवमशेषहेतुम् ।
पश्यन्ति शंभुं कविमीशितारं
रुद्रं बृहन्तं पुरुषं पुराणम् ॥
2.37.m: Gazed upon by the consort of the Supreme Lord, / they beheld within her the God who is the cause of all things— / Śambhu, the sage, the ruler, / Rudra, the immense, ancient Spirit.

2.37.s:
ālokya devīmatha devamīśaṃ
praṇemurānandamavāpuragryam /
jñānaṃ tadaiśaṃ bhagavatprasādā-
dāvirbabhau janmavināśahetu //
2.37.d:
आलोक्य देवीमथ देवमीशं
प्रणेमुरानन्दमवापुरग्र्यम् ।
ज्ञानं तदैशं भगवत्प्रसादा-
दाविर्बभौ जन्मविनाशहेतु ॥
2.37.m: Having beheld the goddess and the Lord, the sovereign god, / they bowed and attained the highest bliss. / Then, by the grace of the Lord, that divine knowledge arose / which brings about the cessation of rebirth.

2.37.s:
iyaṃ hi sā jagato yonirekā
sarvātmikā sarvaniyāmikā ca /
māheśvarīśaktiranādisiddhā
vyomābhidhānā divi rājatīva //
2.37.d:
इयं हि सा जगतो योनिरेका
सर्वात्मिका सर्वनियामिका च ।
माहेश्वरीशक्तिरनादिसिद्धा
व्योमाभिधाना दिवि राजतीव ॥
2.37.m: She indeed is the sole womb of the universe, / the self of all and the controller of all, / the power of the Great Lord, established from beginningless time, / designated as the Void, shining in the heavens.

2.37.s:
asyā mahatparameṣṭhī parastā-
nmaheśvaraḥ śiva eko 'tha rudraḥ /
cakāra viśvaṃ paraśaktiniṣṭhāṃ
māyāmathāruhya sa devadevaḥ //
2.37.d:
अस्या महत्परमेष्ठी परस्ता-
न्महेश्वरः शिव एको ऽथ रुद्रः ।
चकार विश्वं परशक्तिनिष्ठां
मायामथारुह्य स देवदेवः ॥
2.37.m: Beyond her is the supreme lord, the one Śiva, / Maheśvara, and Rudra; / resorting to his illusory creative power, grounded in his transcendent power, / that god of gods fashioned the universe.

2.37.s:
eko devaḥ sarvabhūteṣu gūḍho
māyī rudraḥ sakalo niṣkalaśca /
sa eva devī na ca tadvibhinna-
metajjñātvā hyamṛtatvaṃ vrajanti //
2.37.d:
एको देवः सर्वभूतेषु गूढो
मायी रुद्रः सकलो निष्कलश्च ।
स एव देवी न च तद्विभिन्न-
मेतज्ज्ञात्वा ह्यमृतत्वं व्रजन्ति ॥
2.37.m: The one god, concealed in all beings, / master of illusory creative power, is Rudra, with parts and without parts; / he alone is the goddess, and she is not different from him: / having known this, men indeed go to immortality.

2.37.s:
antarhito 'bhūd bhagavānatheśo
devyā bhargaḥ saha devādidevaḥ /
ārādhayanti sma tameva devaṃ
vanaukasaste punareva rudram //
2.37.d:
अन्तर्हितो ऽभूद् भगवानथेशो
देव्या भर्गः सह देवादिदेवः ।
आराधयन्ति स्म तमेव देवं
वनौकसस्ते पुनरेव रुद्रम् ॥
2.37.m: Then the venerable Lord, Bharga, the supreme god among gods, / vanished together with the goddess. / Those forest-dwellers once again / worshipped that very same god, Rudra.

2.37.s:
etad vaḥ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ devadevaviceṣṭitam /
devadāruvane pūrvaṃ purāṇe yanmayā śrutam //
2.37.d:
एतद् वः कथितं सर्वं देवदेवविचेष्टितम् ।
देवदारुवने पूर्वं पुराणे यन्मया श्रुतम् ॥
2.37.m: All this conduct of the god of gods in the Pine Forest has been related to you, / just as was formerly heard by me in the Purāṇa.

2.37.s:
yaḥ paṭhecchṛṇuyānnityaṃ mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ /
śrāvayed vā dvijān śāntān sa yāti paramāṃ gatim //
iti śrīkūrmapurāṇe ṣaṭsāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāmuparivibhāge saptatriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.37.d:
यः पठेच्छृणुयान्नित्यं मुच्यते सर्वपातकैः ।
श्रावयेद् वा द्विजान् शान्तान् स याति परमां गतिम् ॥
इति श्रीकूर्मपुराणे षट्साहस्त्र्यां संहितायामुपरिविभागे सप्तत्रिंशो ऽध्यायः
2.37.m:
He who recites or constantly listens to it is freed from all sins, / or whoever causes peaceful brahmins to hear it attains the supreme goal.

Thus ends the thirty-seventh chapter in the latter section of the compilation of six thousand verses in the glorious Kūrma Purāṇa.

2.38.s:
sūta uvāca
eṣā puṇyatamā devī devagandharvasevitā /
narmadā lokavikhyātā tīrthānāmuttamā nadī //
2.38.d:
सूत उवाच
एषा पुण्यतमा देवी देवगन्धर्वसेविता ।
नर्मदा लोकविख्याता तीर्थानामुत्तमा नदी ॥
2.38.m: Sūta said: / This most holy goddess, frequented by gods and gandharvas, / is the world-renowned Narmadā, the best of rivers among holy places.

2.38.s:
tasyāḥ śṛṇudhvaṃ māhātmyaṃ mārkaṇḍeyena bhāṣitam /
yudhiṣṭhirāya tu śubhaṃ sarvapāpapraṇāśanam //
2.38.d:
तस्याः शृणुध्वं माहात्म्यं मार्कण्डेयेन भाषितम् ।
युधिष्ठिराय तु शुभं सर्वपापप्रणाशनम् ॥
2.38.m: Hear her auspicious majesty, destructive of all sins, / which was spoken by Mārkaṇḍeya / to Yudhiṣṭhira.

2.38.s:
yudhiṣṭhira uvāca
śrutāstu vividhā dharmāstvatprasādānmahāmune /
māhātmyaṃ ca prayāgasya tīrthāni vividhāni ca //
2.38.d:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच
श्रुतास्तु विविधा धर्मास्त्वत्प्रसादान्महामुने ।
माहात्म्यं च प्रयागस्य तीर्थानि विविधानि च ॥
2.38.m: Yudhiṣṭhira said: / Various duties have been heard by your grace, O great sage, / as well as the majesty of Prayāga and various holy places.

2.38.s:
narmadā sarvatīrthānāṃ mukhyā hi bhavateritā /
tasyāstvidānīṃ māhātmyaṃ vaktumarhasi sattama //
2.38.d:
नर्मदा सर्वतीर्थानां मुख्या हि भवतेरिता ।
तस्यास्त्विदानीं माहात्म्यं वक्तुमर्हसि सत्तम ॥
2.38.m: The Narmadā has indeed been declared by you to be the foremost of all holy places. / Therefore, O best of good men, you should now declare her majesty.

2.38.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
narmadā saritāṃ śreṣṭhā rudradehād viniḥ sṛtā /
tārayet sarvabhūtāni sthāvarāṇi carāṇi ca //
2.38.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच
नर्मदा सरितां श्रेष्ठा रुद्रदेहाद् विनिः सृता ।
तारयेत् सर्वभूतानि स्थावराणि चराणि च ॥
2.38.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / The Narmadā, the best of rivers, issued from the body of Rudra; / she delivers all beings, both stationary and moving.

2.38.s:
narmadāyāstu māhātmyaṃ purāṇe yanmayā śrutam /
idānīṃ tatpravakṣyāmi śṛṇuṣvaikamanāḥ śubham //
2.38.d:
नर्मदायास्तु माहात्म्यं पुराणे यन्मया श्रुतम् ।
इदानीं तत्प्रवक्ष्यामि शृणुष्वैकमनाः शुभम् ॥
2.38.m: Now I shall proclaim the auspicious majesty of the Narmadā / which was heard by me in the Purāṇa; / listen with a single mind.

2.38.s:
puṇyā kanakhale gaṅgā kurukṣetre sarasvatī /
grāme vā yadi vāraṇye puṇyā sarvatra narmadā //
2.38.d:
पुण्या कनखले गङ्गा कुरुक्षेत्रे सरस्वती ।
ग्रामे वा यदि वारण्ये पुण्या सर्वत्र नर्मदा ॥
2.38.m: The Gaṅgā is holy at Kanakhala, the Sarasvatī at Kurukṣetra, / but whether in a village or in a forest, the Narmadā is holy everywhere.

2.38.s:
tribhiḥ sārasvataṃ toyaṃ saptāhena tu yāmunam /
sadyaḥ punāti gāṅgeyaṃ darśanādeva nārmadam //
2.38.d:
त्रिभिः सारस्वतं तोयं सप्ताहेन तु यामुनम् ।
सद्यः पुनाति गाङ्गेयं दर्शनादेव नार्मदम् ॥
2.38.m: The water of the Sarasvatī purifies in three days, that of the Yamunā in seven, / that of the Gaṅgā immediately, but that of the Narmadā by mere sight.

2.38.s:
kaliṅgadeśapaścārdhe parvate 'marakaṇṭake /
puṇyā ca triṣu lokeṣu ramaṇīyā manoramā //
2.38.d:
कलिङ्गदेशपश्चार्धे पर्वते ऽमरकण्टके ।
पुण्या च त्रिषु लोकेषु रमणीया मनोरमा ॥
2.38.m: In the western half of the Kaliṅga country, on Mount Amarakaṇṭaka, / she is holy in the three worlds, delightful and captivating.

2.38.s:
sadevāsuragandharvā ṛṣayaśca tapodhanāḥ /
tapastaptvā tu rājendra siddhiṃ tu paramāṃ gatāḥ //
2.38.d:
सदेवासुरगन्धर्वा ऋषयश्च तपोधनाः ।
तपस्तप्त्वा तु राजेन्द्र सिद्धिं तु परमां गताः ॥
2.38.m: Gods, asuras, and gandharvas, as well as sages rich in asceticism, / having performed ascetic penance there, O best of kings, have attained supreme perfection.

2.38.s:
tatra snātvā naro rājan niyamastho jitendriyaḥ /
upoṣya rajanīmekāṃ kulānāṃ tārayecchatam //
2.38.d:
तत्र स्नात्वा नरो राजन् नियमस्थो जितेन्द्रियः ।
उपोष्य रजनीमेकां कुलानां तारयेच्छतम् ॥
2.38.m: Having bathed there, O king, observing vows and with senses conquered, / fasting for a single night, a man delivers a hundred generations of his family.

2.38.s:
yojanānāṃ śataṃ sāgraṃ śrūyate sariduttamā /
vistāreṇa tu rājendra yojanadvayamāyatā //
2.38.d:
योजनानां शतं साग्रं श्रूयते सरिदुत्तमा ।
विस्तारेण तु राजेन्द्र योजनद्वयमायता ॥
2.38.m: This best of rivers is heard to be more than a hundred leagues [in length], / and in breadth, O king of kings, two leagues wide.

2.38.s:
ṣaṣṭitīrthasahasrāṇi ṣaṣṭikoṭyastathaiva ca /
parvatasya samantāt tu tiṣṭhantyamarakaṇṭake //
2.38.d:
षष्टितीर्थसहस्राणि षष्टिकोट्यस्तथैव च ।
पर्वतस्य समन्तात् तु तिष्ठन्त्यमरकण्टके ॥
2.38.m: Sixty thousand and sixty crore holy places / are situated on all sides around the mountain at Amarakaṇṭaka.

2.38.s:
brahmacārī śucirbhūtvā jitakrodho jitendriyaḥ /
sarvahiṃsānivṛttastu sarvabhūtahite rataḥ //
2.38.d:
ब्रह्मचारी शुचिर्भूत्वा जितक्रोधो जितेन्द्रियः ।
सर्वहिंसानिवृत्तस्तु सर्वभूतहिते रतः ॥
2.38.m: Becoming a celibate student, pure, with anger conquered and senses restrained, / turned away from all violence, and devoted to the welfare of all beings,

2.38.s:
evaṃ sarvasamācāro yastu prāṇān samutsṛjet /
tasya puṇyaphalaṃ rājan śṛṇuṣvāvahito nṛpa //
2.38.d:
एवं सर्वसमाचारो यस्तु प्राणान् समुत्सृजेत् ।
तस्य पुण्यफलं राजन् शृणुष्वावहितो नृप ॥
2.38.m: one of such conduct who gives up his vital breaths— / listen attentively, O king, to the fruit of his merit:

2.38.s:
śatavarṣasahasrāṇi svarge modati pāṇḍava /
sapsarogaṇasaṃkīrṇo divyastrīparivāritaḥ //
2.38.d:
शतवर्षसहस्राणि स्वर्गे मोदति पाण्डव ।
सप्सरोगणसंकीर्णो दिव्यस्त्रीपरिवारितः ॥
2.38.m: For a hundred thousand years he rejoices in heaven, O son of Pāṇḍu, / crowded about by hosts of apsarases and surrounded by celestial women.

2.38.s:
divyagandhānuliptaśca divyapuṣpopaśobhitaḥ /
krīḍate devaloke tu daivataiḥ saha modate //
2.38.d:
दिव्यगन्धानुलिप्तश्च दिव्यपुष्पोपशोभितः ।
क्रीडते देवलोके तु दैवतैः सह मोदते ॥
2.38.m: Anointed with divine perfumes and adorned with heavenly flowers, / he sports in the world of the gods and rejoices together with deities.

2.38.s:
tataḥ svargāt paribhraṣṭo rājā bhavati dhārmikaḥ /
gṛhaṃ tu labhate 'sau vai nānāratnasamanvitam //
2.38.d:
ततः स्वर्गात् परिभ्रष्टो राजा भवति धार्मिकः ।
गृहं तु लभते ऽसौ वै नानारत्नसमन्वितम् ॥
2.38.m: Then, falling from heaven, he becomes a righteous king; / he obtains a mansion furnished with diverse gems,

2.38.s:
stambhairmaṇimayairdivyairvajravaidūryabhūṣitam /
ālekhyavāhanaiḥ śubhrairdāsīdāsasamanvitam //
2.38.d:
स्तम्भैर्मणिमयैर्दिव्यैर्वज्रवैदूर्यभूषितम् ।
आलेख्यवाहनैः शुभ्रैर्दासीदाससमन्वितम् ॥
2.38.m: adorned with divine jeweled pillars, diamonds, and lapis lazuli, / with paintings, white vehicles, and maidservants and manservants.

2.38.s:
rājarājeśvaraḥ śrīmān sarvastrījanavallabhaḥ /
jīved varṣaśataṃ sāgraṃ tatra bhogasamanvitaḥ //
2.38.d:
राजराजेश्वरः श्रीमान् सर्वस्त्रीजनवल्लभः ।
जीवेद् वर्षशतं साग्रं तत्र भोगसमन्वितः ॥
2.38.m: A king of kings, majestic, beloved by all women, / endowed with enjoyments, he lives there for a full hundred years.

2.38.s:
agnipraveśe 'tha jale athavānaśane kṛte /
anivartikā gatistasya pavanasyāmbare yathā //
2.38.d:
अग्निप्रवेशे ऽथ जले अथवानशने कृते ।
अनिवर्तिका गतिस्तस्य पवनस्याम्बरे यथा ॥
2.38.m: If he enters fire, or water, or performs death by starvation, / his course is non-returning, like that of the wind in the sky.

2.38.s:
paścime parvatataṭe sarvapāpavināśanaḥ /
hrado jaleśvaro nāma triṣu lokeṣu viśrutaḥ //
2.38.d:
पश्चिमे पर्वततटे सर्वपापविनाशनः ।
ह्रदो जलेश्वरो नाम त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतः ॥
2.38.m: On the western slope of the mountain is a pool named Jaleśvara, / destroying all sins, renowned in the three worlds.

2.38.s:
tatra piṇḍapradānena saṃdhyopāsanakarmaṇā /
daśavarṣāṇi pitarastarpitāḥ syurna saṃśayaḥ //
2.38.d:
तत्र पिण्डप्रदानेन संध्योपासनकर्मणा ।
दशवर्षाणि पितरस्तर्पिताः स्युर्न संशयः ॥
2.38.m: By offering rice balls there and by the rite of twilight devotion, / the ancestors will be gratified for ten years; there is no doubt.

2.38.s:
dakṣiṇe narmadākūle kapilākhyā mahānadī /
saralārjunasaṃcchannā nātidūre vyavasthitā //
2.38.d:
दक्षिणे नर्मदाकूले कपिलाख्या महानदी ।
सरलार्जुनसंच्छन्ना नातिदूरे व्यवस्थिता ॥
2.38.m: On the south bank of the Narmadā, not very far away, / is situated a great river named Kapilā, covered with pine and arjuna trees.

2.38.s:
sā tu puṇyā mahābhāgā triṣu lokeṣu viśrutā /
tatra koṭiśataṃ sāgraṃ tīrthānāṃ tu yudhiṣṭhira //
2.38.d:
सा तु पुण्या महाभागा त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुता ।
तत्र कोटिशतं साग्रं तीर्थानां तु युधिष्ठिर ॥
2.38.m: She is holy, highly fortunate, renowned throughout the three worlds; / there are over a billion holy places there, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

2.38.s:
tasmiṃstīrthe tu ye vṛkṣāḥ patitāḥ kālaparyayāt /
narmadātoyasaṃspṛṣṭāste yānti paramāṃ gatim //
2.38.d:
तस्मिंस्तीर्थे तु ये वृक्षाः पतिताः कालपर्ययात् ।
नर्मदातोयसंस्पृष्टास्ते यान्ति परमां गतिम् ॥
2.38.m: Whatever trees have fallen at that holy place in the course of time, / when touched by the waters of the Narmadā, go to the supreme state.

2.38.s:
dvitīyā tu mahābhāgā viśalyakaraṇī śubhā /
tatra tīrthe naraḥ snātvā viśalyo bhavati kṣaṇāt //
2.38.d:
द्वितीया तु महाभागा विशल्यकरणी शुभा ।
तत्र तीर्थे नरः स्नात्वा विशल्यो भवति क्षणात् ॥
2.38.m: A second, highly auspicious and fortunate [river] is the Viśalyakaraṇī; / bathing at that holy place, a man becomes free from grief in an instant.

2.38.s:
kapilā ca viśalyā ca śrūyate rājasattama /
īśvareṇa purā proktā lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā //
2.38.d:
कपिला च विशल्या च श्रूयते राजसत्तम ।
ईश्वरेण पुरा प्रोक्ता लोकानां हितकाम्यया ॥
2.38.m: The Kapilā and the Viśalyā, O best of kings, are traditionally heard / to have been spoken of of old by the Lord out of a desire for the welfare of the worlds.

2.38.s:
anāśakaṃ tu yaḥ kuryāt tasmiṃstīrthe narādhipa /
sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā rudralokaṃ sa gacchati //
2.38.d:
अनाशकं तु यः कुर्यात् तस्मिंस्तीर्थे नराधिप ।
सर्वपापविशुद्धात्मा रुद्रलोकं स गच्छति ॥
2.38.m: Whosoever undertakes fasting to death at that holy place, O king, / his soul purified of all sins, goes to the realm of Rudra.

2.38.s:
tatra snātvā naro rājannaśvamedhaphalaṃ labhet /
ye vasantyuttare kūle rudraloke vasanti te //
2.38.d:
तत्र स्नात्वा नरो राजन्नश्वमेधफलं लभेत् ।
ये वसन्त्युत्तरे कूले रुद्रलोके वसन्ति ते ॥
2.38.m: Bathing there, O king, a man obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice; / those who reside on its northern bank dwell in the realm of Rudra.

2.38.s:
sarasvatyāṃ ca gaṅgāyāṃ narmadāyāṃ yudhiṣṭhira /
samaṃ snānaṃ ca dānaṃ ca yathā me śaṅkaro 'bravīt //
2.38.d:
सरस्वत्यां च गङ्गायां नर्मदायां युधिष्ठिर ।
समं स्नानं च दानं च यथा मे शङ्करो ऽब्रवीत् ॥
2.38.m: At the Sarasvatī, the Gaṅgā, and the Narmadā, O Yudhiṣṭhira, / bathing and giving are equal, just as Śaṅkara told me.

2.38.s:
parityajati yaḥ praṇān parvate 'marakaṇṭake /
varṣakoṭiśataṃ sāgraṃ rudraloke mahīyate //
2.38.d:
परित्यजति यः प्रणान् पर्वते ऽमरकण्टके ।
वर्षकोटिशतं साग्रं रुद्रलोके महीयते ॥
2.38.m: He who relinquishes his life breaths on Mount Amarakaṇṭaka / is glorified in the world of Rudra for over a thousand million years.

2.38.s:
narmadāyāṃ jalaṃ puṇyaṃ phenormisamalaṅkṛtam /
pavitraṃ śirasā vandya sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate //
2.38.d:
नर्मदायां जलं पुण्यं फेनोर्मिसमलङ्कृतम् ।
पवित्रं शिरसा वन्द्य सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥
2.38.m: The holy water in the Narmadā, adorned with waves of foam, / is pure; revering it with one's head, one is freed from all sins.

2.38.s:
narmadā sarvataḥ puṇyā brahmahatyāpahāriṇī /
ahorātropavāsena mucyate brahmahatyayā //
2.38.d:
नर्मदा सर्वतः पुण्या ब्रह्महत्यापहारिणी ।
अहोरात्रोपवासेन मुच्यते ब्रह्महत्यया ॥
2.38.m: The Narmadā is holy everywhere, removing [the guilt of] killing a brahmin; / by fasting for a day and night, one is freed from killing a brahmin.

2.38.s:
jāleśvaraṃ tīrthavaraṃ sarvapāpavināśanam /
tatra gatvā niyamavān sarvakāmāṃllabhennaraḥ //
2.38.d:
जालेश्वरं तीर्थवरं सर्वपापविनाशनम् ।
तत्र गत्वा नियमवान् सर्वकामांल्लभेन्नरः ॥
2.38.m: Jāleśvara is an excellent holy place, destroying all sins; / going there with observed vows, a man obtains all desires.

2.38.s:
candrasūryoparāge tu gatvā hyamarakaṇṭakam /
aśvamedhād daśaguṇaṃ puṇyamāpnoti mānavaḥ //
2.38.d:
चन्द्रसूर्योपरागे तु गत्वा ह्यमरकण्टकम् ।
अश्वमेधाद् दशगुणं पुण्यमाप्नोति मानवः ॥
2.38.m: Going to Amarakaṇṭaka during an eclipse of the moon or the sun, / a human being attains tenfold the merit of a horse sacrifice.

2.38.s:
eṣa puṇyo girivaro devagandharvasevitaḥ /
nānādrumalatākīrṇo nānāpuṣpopaśobhitaḥ //
2.38.d:
एष पुण्यो गिरिवरो देवगन्धर्वसेवितः ।
नानाद्रुमलताकीर्णो नानापुष्पोपशोभितः ॥
2.38.m: This holy, best of mountains, resorted to by gods and gandharvas, / is filled with various trees and creepers, and adorned with various flowers.

2.38.s:
tatra saṃnihito rājan devyā saha maheśvaraḥ /
brahmā viṣṇustathā cendro vidyādharagaṇaiḥ saha //
2.38.d:
तत्र संनिहितो राजन् देव्या सह महेश्वरः ।
ब्रह्मा विष्णुस्तथा चेन्द्रो विद्याधरगणैः सह ॥
2.38.m: Present there, O king, is Maheśvara together with the goddess, / as well as Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Indra, together with the troops of vidyādharas.

2.38.s:
pradakṣiṇaṃ tu yaḥ kuryāt parvataṃ hyamarakaṇṭakam /
pauṇḍarīkasya yajñasya phalaṃ prāpnoti mānaḥ //
2.38.d:
प्रदक्षिणं तु यः कुर्यात् पर्वतं ह्यमरकण्टकम् ।
पौण्डरीकस्य यज्ञस्य फलं प्राप्नोति मानः ॥
2.38.m: A mortal who circumambulates Mount Amarakaṇṭaka / obtains the fruit of the Pauṇḍarīka sacrifice.

2.38.s:
kāverī nāma vipulā nadī kalpaṣanāśinī /
tatra snātvā mahādevamarcayed vṛṣabhadhvajam /
saṃgame narmadāyāstu rudraloke mahīyate //
iti śrīkūrmapurāṇe ṣaṭsāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāmuparivibhāge aṣṭātriśo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.38.d:
कावेरी नाम विपुला नदी कल्पषनाशिनी ।
तत्र स्नात्वा महादेवमर्चयेद् वृषभध्वजम् ।
संगमे नर्मदायास्तु रुद्रलोके महीयते ॥
इति श्रीकूर्मपुराणे षट्साहस्त्र्यां संहितायामुपरिविभागे अष्टात्रिशो ऽध्यायः
2.38.m:
There is a broad river named Kāverī, destroying sins; / having bathed there and worshipped Mahādeva, whose emblem is a bull, / at the confluence of the Narmadā, one is glorified in the realm of Rudra.

Thus ends the thirty-eighth chapter in the latter section of the compilation of six thousand verses in the glorious Kūrma Purāṇa.

2.39.s:
mārkaṇḍeya uvāca
narmadā saritāṃ śreṣṭhā sarvapāpavināśinī /
munibhiḥ kathitā pūrvamīśvareṇa svayaṃbhuvā //
2.39.d:
मार्कण्डेय उवाच
नर्मदा सरितां श्रेष्ठा सर्वपापविनाशिनी ।
मुनिभिः कथिता पूर्वमीश्वरेण स्वयंभुवा ॥
2.39.m: Mārkaṇḍeya said: / The Narmadā is the best of rivers, destroying all sins; / it was spoken of formerly by the sages and by the self-existent Lord.

2.39.s:
munibhiḥ saṃstutā hyeṣā narmadā pravarā nadī /
rudragātrād viniṣkrāntā lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā //
2.39.d:
मुनिभिः संस्तुता ह्येषा नर्मदा प्रवरा नदी ।
रुद्रगात्राद् विनिष्क्रान्ता लोकानां हितकाम्यया ॥
2.39.m: This excellent river Narmadā was indeed praised by the sages; / it emerged from the body of Rudra out of desire for the welfare of the worlds.

2.39.s:
sarvapāpaharā nityaṃ sarvadevanamaskṛtā /
saṃstutā devagandharvairapyarobhistathaiva ca //
2.39.d:
सर्वपापहरा नित्यं सर्वदेवनमस्कृता ।
संस्तुता देवगन्धर्वैरप्यरोभिस्तथैव च ॥
2.39.m: It always removes all sins and is bowed to by all gods; / it is praised by gods, gandharvas, and likewise by apsarases.

2.39.s:
uttare caiva tatkūle tīrthaṃ trailokyaviśrutam /
nāmnā bhadreśvaraṃ puṇyaṃ sarvapāpaharaṃ śubham /
tatra snātvā naro rājan daivataiḥ saha mohate //
2.39.d:
उत्तरे चैव तत्कूले तीर्थं त्रैलोक्यविश्रुतम् ।
नाम्ना भद्रेश्वरं पुण्यं सर्वपापहरं शुभम् ।
तत्र स्नात्वा नरो राजन् दैवतैः सह मोहते ॥
2.39.m: And on its northern bank is a pilgrimage site renowned throughout the three worlds, / named Bhadreśvara, holy, removing all sins, and auspicious; / bathing there, O king, a man rejoices along with the gods.

2.39.s:
tato gaccheta rājendra tīrthamāmrātakeśvaram /
tatra snātvā naro rājan gosahasraphalaṃ labhet //
2.39.d:
ततो गच्छेत राजेन्द्र तीर्थमाम्रातकेश्वरम् ।
तत्र स्नात्वा नरो राजन् गोसहस्रफलं लभेत् ॥
2.39.m: Then one should go, O best of kings, to the pilgrimage site Āmrātakeśvara; / bathing there, O king, a man obtains the fruit of [donating] a thousand cows.

2.39.s:
tato 'ṅgāreśvaraṃ gacchenniyato niyatāśanaḥ /
sarvapāpaviśuddhātmā rudraloke mahīyate //
2.39.d:
ततो ऽङ्गारेश्वरं गच्छेन्नियतो नियताशनः ।
सर्वपापविशुद्धात्मा रुद्रलोके महीयते ॥
2.39.m: Then, restrained and eating measured food, one should go to Aṅgāreśvara; / his soul purified of all sins, he is glorified in the realm of Rudra.

2.39.s:
tato gaccheta rājendra kedāraṃ nāma puṇyadam /
tatra snātvodakaṃ kṛtvā sarvān kāmānavāpnuyāt //
2.39.d:
ततो गच्छेत राजेन्द्र केदारं नाम पुण्यदम् ।
तत्र स्नात्वोदकं कृत्वा सर्वान् कामानवाप्नुयात् ॥
2.39.m: Then one should go, O best of kings, to the merit-yielding place called Kedāra; / having bathed there and offered water, one obtains all desires.

2.39.s:
pippaleśaṃ tato gacchet sarvapāpavināśanam /
tatra snātvā mahārāja rudraloke mahīyate //
2.39.d:
पिप्पलेशं ततो गच्छेत् सर्वपापविनाशनम् ।
तत्र स्नात्वा महाराज रुद्रलोके महीयते ॥
2.39.m: Then one should go to Pippaleśa, which destroys all sins; / bathing there, O great king, he is glorified in the realm of Rudra.

2.39.s:
tato gaccheta rājendra vimaleśvaramuttamam /
tatra prāṇān parityajya rudralokamavāpnuyāt //
2.39.d:
ततो गच्छेत राजेन्द्र विमलेश्वरमुत्तमम् ।
तत्र प्राणान् परित्यज्य रुद्रलोकमवाप्नुयात् ॥
2.39.m: Then one should go, O best of kings, to supreme Vimaleśvara; / giving up one's life-breaths there, one attains the realm of Rudra.

2.39.s:
tataḥ puṣkariṇīṃ gacchet snānaṃ tatra samācaret /
snātamātro narastatra indrasyārdhāsanaṃ labhet //
2.39.d:
ततः पुष्करिणीं गच्छेत् स्नानं तत्र समाचरेत् ।
स्नातमात्रो नरस्तत्र इन्द्रस्यार्धासनं लभेत् ॥
2.39.m: Then one should go to Puṣkariṇī and perform a bath there; / merely by bathing there, a man obtains half of Indra's throne.

2.39.s:
tato gaccheta rājendra śūlabhedamiti śrutam /
tatra snātvārcayed devaṃ gosahasraphalaṃ labhet //
2.39.d:
ततो गच्छेत राजेन्द्र शूलभेदमिति श्रुतम् ।
तत्र स्नात्वार्चयेद् देवं गोसहस्रफलं लभेत् ॥
2.39.m: Then one should go, O best of kings, to that which is known as Śūlabheda; / bathing there and worshiping the god, one obtains the fruit of [donating] a thousand cows.

2.39.s:
tato gaccheta rājendra balitīrthamanuttam /
tatra snātvā naro rājan sihāsanapatirbhavet //
2.39.d:
ततो गच्छेत राजेन्द्र बलितीर्थमनुत्तम् ।
तत्र स्नात्वा नरो राजन् सिहासनपतिर्भवेत् ॥
2.39.m: Then one should go, O best of kings, to the unsurpassed Balitīrtha; / bathing there, O king, a man becomes the master of a throne.

2.39.s:
śakratīrthaṃ tato gacchet kūle caiva tu dakṣiṇe /
upoṣya rajanīmekāṃ snānaṃ kṛtvā yathāvidhi //
2.39.d:
शक्रतीर्थं ततो गच्छेत् कूले चैव तु दक्षिणे ।
उपोष्य रजनीमेकां स्नानं कृत्वा यथाविधि ॥
2.39.m: Then one should go to Śakratīrtha, on the southern bank; / fasting for one night and performing a bath according to the rule,

2.39.s:
ārādhayenmahāyogaṃ devaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ harim /
gosahasraphalaṃ prāpya viṣṇulokaṃ sa gacchati //
2.39.d:
आराधयेन्महायोगं देवं नारायणं हरिम् ।
गोसहस्रफलं प्राप्य विष्णुलोकं स गच्छति ॥
2.39.m: one should venerate God Nārāyaṇa, Hari, the Great Yoga; / obtaining the fruit of [donating] a thousand cows, he goes to the realm of Viṣṇu.

2.39.s:
ṛṣitīrthaṃ tato gatvā sarvapāpaharaṃ nṛṇām /
snātamātro narastatra śivaloke mahīyate //
2.39.d:
ऋषितीर्थं ततो गत्वा सर्वपापहरं नृणाम् ।
स्नातमात्रो नरस्तत्र शिवलोके महीयते ॥
2.39.m: Then, going to Ṛṣitīrtha, which takes away all sins of mortals, / merely by bathing there, a man is glorified in the realm of Śiva.

2.39.s:
nāradasya tu tatraiva tīrthaṃ paramaśobhanam /
snātamātro narastatra gosahasraphalaṃ labhet //
2.39.d:
नारदस्य तु तत्रैव तीर्थं परमशोभनम् ।
स्नातमात्रो नरस्तत्र गोसहस्रफलं लभेत् ॥
2.39.m: And right there is the supremely splendid pilgrimage site of Nārada; / merely by bathing there, a man obtains the fruit of [donating] a thousand cows.

2.39.s:
yatra taptaṃ tapaḥ pūrvaṃ nāradena surarṣiṇā /
pratīstasya dadau yogaṃ devadevo maheśvaraḥ //
2.39.d:
यत्र तप्तं तपः पूर्वं नारदेन सुरर्षिणा ।
प्रतीस्तस्य ददौ योगं देवदेवो महेश्वरः ॥
2.39.m: Where austerities were formerly performed by the celestial sage Nārada, / pleased with him, the God of gods, Maheśvara, granted yoga.

2.39.s:
brahmaṇā nirmitaṃ liṅgaṃ brahmeśvaramiti śrutam /
yatra snātvā naro rājan brahmaloke mahīyate //
2.39.d:
ब्रह्मणा निर्मितं लिङ्गं ब्रह्मेश्वरमिति श्रुतम् ।
यत्र स्नात्वा नरो राजन् ब्रह्मलोके महीयते ॥
2.39.m: The liṅga fashioned by Brahmā is known as Brahmeśvara; / bathing where, O king, a man is glorified in the realm of Brahmā.

2.39.s:
ṛṇatīrthaṃ tato gacchet sa ṛṇānmucyate dhruvam /
maheśvaraṃ tato gacchet paryāptaṃ janmanaḥ phalam //
2.39.d:
ऋणतीर्थं ततो गच्छेत् स ऋणान्मुच्यते ध्रुवम् ।
महेश्वरं ततो गच्छेत् पर्याप्तं जन्मनः फलम् ॥
2.39.m: Then one should go to Ṛṇatīrtha; he is certainly freed from debt; / then one should go to Maheśvara: the fruit of one's birth is complete.

2.39.s:
bhīmeśvaraṃ tato gacchet sarvavyādhivināśanam /
snātamātro narastatra sarvaduḥkhaiḥ pramucyate //
2.39.d:
भीमेश्वरं ततो गच्छेत् सर्वव्याधिविनाशनम् ।
स्नातमात्रो नरस्तत्र सर्वदुःखैः प्रमुच्यते ॥
2.39.m: Then one should go to Bhīmeśvara, which destroys all diseases; / merely by bathing there, a man is freed from all suffering.

2.39.s:
tato gaccheta rājendra piṅgaleśvaramuttamam /
